meta.spec_reference: PKWARE APPNOTE.TXT v6.3.10 - .ZIP File Format Specification (including the ZIP64 application note and the WinZip AE-1/AE-2 extension for extra field 0x9901); RFC 1951 (DEFLATE) and RFC 1950 (zlib) for method 8; CRC-32/ISO-HDLC per ISO 3309 / ITU-T V.42; Info-ZIP unzip 6.0, libzip and minizip-ng decoder behaviour; template header: 010 Editor ZIPAdv.bt v2.6 (2015-07-18), SweetScape Software

schema_extensions.name: evidence.note carried alongside evidence.line / evidence.snippet
schema_extensions.why: ZIP pins many values that the .bt declares but never states as a literal (VendorID "AE", efVersion 1, the CRC-32 polynomial). For source "both" entries the object carries the verbatim .bt line AND the specification rule in one place, so the constraint stays grounded in both sources without duplicating entries.

schema_extensions.name: lookahead.function values "ReadUInt" and "FindFirst", plus lookahead.snippet / lookahead.note
schema_extensions.why: The top-level dispatcher decides every record type with 'tag = ReadUInt( FTell() );' (line 618) and compares it against the seven SignatureTYPE literals (lines 624-659), aborting with Warning + return -1 otherwise (lines 664-667). Neither the 32-bit unsigned read nor the forward signature scan at line 468 (FindFirst(S_ZIPDATADESCR,...)) is among the four function names the schema lists, yet both are exactly the call sites FormatFuzzer mines for good known values. The schema's own keys (function, call_site_line, values, preferred) are kept unchanged; "snippet" and "note" are added inside the same object so the mined value set stays attached to the verbatim .bt line it came from. Recording FindFirst on ZIPDATADESCR.ddSignature rather than inventing a field keeps one entry per field, as the schema requires.

schema_extensions.name: dependencies[].when.bit_set / when.bit_clear
schema_extensions.why: ZIPFILERECORD.frFlags and ZIPDIRENTRY.deFlags are bitmasks, so the governing conditions are per-bit tests (bit 3 = data descriptor present, bit 0 = encrypted, bit 6 = strong encryption, bit 11 = UTF-8 names) rather than equals / in / min / max.

schema_extensions.name: payload_wellformedness.codec_by_value
schema_extensions.why: frData's required internal structure is selected by another field (ZIPFILERECORD.frCompression), so a single 'codec' string cannot describe it. The per-method map keeps one entry per field, as the schema requires, while naming every codec the enum can select and giving a concrete generation strategy for each one a generator can actually emit.

schema_extensions.name: meta.typedef_enum_coverage
schema_extensions.why: Checklist item 4 requires an audit of every typedef enum. Two of ZIP's enums are recorded on their fields with a type other than enumerated_values (SignatureTYPE fields are Tier A fixed_value because the dispatcher aborts on any other value; FLAGTYPE and FILEATTRIBUTE are bitmask_constraint because they are bitfields, not selectors), so an explicit map from enum typename to the entries carrying its legal set documents the reason instead of silently deviating.

schema_extensions.name: constraints.*.repeat_of / min_repeat / max_repeat
schema_extensions.why: Eleven Tier C fields are variable-length runs whose only requirement is that their byte count equals another field: frFileName, deFileName, deFileComment, elComment, dsData, ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.DataSect, the two EXTRAFIELD chains, and the three StrongEncryptedHeader blobs (IVData, ErdData, VData). repeat_of names the governing length field so a template author wires the array size to it instead of guessing; min_repeat/max_repeat state the record-count floor and ceiling of the two extra-field chains (0 and unbounded). Neither key narrows a value - all eleven entries stay type unconstrained, Tier C - and the byte count itself is enforced by the Tier A calculated_value entry on the length field named by repeat_of.

schema_extensions.name: constraints.*.min_value / max_value
schema_extensions.why: Annotations on Tier A calculated_value and Tier B entries only; they never appear on a Tier C field and never narrow a legal set. max_value is always the field's own declared width (65535 for a ushort, 4294967295 for a uint), recording that the length or count fills its type rather than capping it below that; min_value is either 0, the unsigned floor, or the APPNOTE structural floor of 44 bytes on ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64DirectoryRecordSize, below which the ZIP64 end record cannot hold its own fixed members. What a generator may emit is still fixed solely by algorithm/covers/depends_on (Tier A) or valid_values (Tier B).

schema_extensions.name: constraints.*.bit_names and constraints.*.completeness_reason
schema_extensions.why: bit_names gives the template's own member name for each entry of valid_bits on the four bitmask_constraint fields (FLAGTYPE for frFlags and deFlags, the APPNOTE internal-attribute bits for the plain ushort deInternalAttributes, FILEATTRIBUTE for deExternalAttributes), supplying for bitmasks the parallel naming the schema asks for with value_names on enumerations. completeness_reason carries the 'and if partial, why' half the schema requires next to completeness, as its own key, so the eleven partial entries - all 65536 flag combinations, or a multi-volume disk-number range a single-volume generator never reaches - can state exactly what is and is not excluded.

meta.structure_note: ZIP is a little-endian stream of self-describing records: N x (ZIPFILERECORD local header + extra-field chain + compressed payload + optional ZIPDATADESCR), then a contiguous central directory of N x ZIPDIRENTRY, then the optional ZIP64 tail (ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD followed by ZIP64ENDLOCATOR), then the mandatory ZIPENDLOCATOR as the last record with its archive comment after it, with ZIPDIGITALSIG records permitted after local records and after the central directory; the format does have a compressed/encoded payload and it is ZIPFILERECORD.frData, whose codec is chosen by ZIPFILERECORD.frCompression (0 = stored, 8 = raw RFC 1951 deflate, plus Deflate64/bzip2/LZMA/PPMd/WavPack/JPEG/WinZip-AE), while every other opaque byte run in the template (dsData, DataSect, CertData, efData, comments, file names) is free-form and unchecked.

typedef_enum_coverage.recorded_as: Tier A fixed_value, one pinned member per field, with all seven members enumerated in each entry's notes and in the line-618 ReadUInt lookahead
typedef_enum_coverage.why_not_enumerated_values: Each field's value is fixed by the record it heads, and the top-level dispatcher refuses the whole file on any other value (lines 664-667). That is the Tier A test verbatim, so the enum's cross-field union is not a per-field legal set.

typedef_enum_coverage.recorded_as: Tier B bitmask_constraint over all 16 named bits
typedef_enum_coverage.why_not_enumerated_values: It is a bitmask, not a selector: every combination of the 16 bits is a distinct legal value, so bitmask_constraint is the faithful type. No member was dropped.

typedef_enum_coverage.recorded_as: Tier B bitmask_constraint over all 44 named members (9 DOS attribute bits, 10 high-word Unix file-type bits, 9 Unix permission bits, 4 Unix reserved bits, 12 UnixFile* aliases)
typedef_enum_coverage.why_not_enumerated_values: It is a bitmask, not a selector; the enum's members are individual bits that combine. No member was dropped.

typedef_enum_coverage.recorded_as: Not an enum in the .bt (typedef byte); recorded Tier B enumerated_values from the APPNOTE version table

axis_coverage.reason: All eight belong to EXTRA64FIELD, the ZIP64 variant of the extra-field reader declared at lines 289-313 whose only instantiation site is commented out at lines 542-547 (see unused_declarations): both live chains - lines 406-411 in ZIPFILERECORD and lines 501-506 in ZIPDIRENTRY - instantiate EXTRAFIELD, so an axis sampling the EXTRA64FIELD members would emit bytes no reader path in this template consumes. The entries are retained as documentation of the declaration. Every other constraint key is named by exactly one axis, and each Tier C field and each field appearing in a payload_wellformedness.derives_from either has its own axis or is covered by the axis of the field that governs it.

unused_declarations.name: EXTRA64FIELD
unused_declarations.note: Declared as the ZIP64 variant of the extra-field reader (uint64 efOriginalSize and efCompressedSize, with efHeaderOffset and efDiskNumberStart commented out at lines 299-300) but never instantiated: its only call site, the loop over the ZIP64 end record's data section, is commented out at lines 542-547, so those trailing bytes are read as ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.DataSect instead. The eight EXTRA64FIELD.* constraint entries document the declaration and the APPNOTE 0x0001 / 0x7075 layouts, but a generator must not emit them and no diversity axis samples them.

unused_declarations.name: read_VERSIONTYPE / read_VERECORD / read_FLAGTYPE / read_EXTRAFIELD / read_FILEATTRIBUTE / ReadZIPFILERECORD / ReadZIPDIRENTRY / WriteZIPFILERECORD
unused_declarations.note: 010 Editor display and tree-write helpers: the read= functions build strings for the template tree and the write= function copies an edited name back into frFileName. They parse no input bytes and declare no fields, so they carry no constraints of their own. They remain the evidence for several rules - the bit loop at lines 135-148 in read_FLAGTYPE for the bitmask semantics of frFlags/deFlags, the same loop at lines 362-377 in read_FILEATTRIBUTE for the DOS/Unix attribute split, and ReadZIPFILERECORD (579-585) / ReadZIPDIRENTRY (587-593) for the fact that the entry name is the value a user sees in the tree.

VERECORD.Version.tier_rationale: A wrong version byte does not make a conforming decoder refuse the file - Info-ZIP unzip only emits its 'ZIP file version N.N unsupported' warning (error = PK_WARN) and keeps extracting - so it fails the Tier A test, but its legal set is the finite APPNOTE version table, which is Tier B.
VERECORD.Version.description: The version-made-by / version-needed-to-extract byte (major*10 + minor); it is legal when it names a ZIP feature level the entry actually uses.

evidence.note: APPNOTE 6.3.10 'Version Needed To Extract' / 'Version Made By' table: 10, 11, 20, 21, 25, 27, 45, 46, 50, 51, 52, 61, 62, 63. The .bt renders it as a decimal via SPrintf("%1.1f", af/10) at line 71 and never compares it against a literal.

VERECORD.Version.notes: One typename covers all five instantiation sites: ZIPFILERECORD.frVersion, ZIPDIRENTRY.deVersionMadeBy, ZIPDIRENTRY.deVersionToExtract, ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64VersionMadeBy and ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64VersionToExtract. 20 covers stored/deflate entries, 45 is required the moment a ZIP64 extra field carries a size, and 46/50/51/63 are required for bzip2/DES/AES/LZMA-PPMd-AE respectively (see dependencies).

VERECORD.HostOS.tier_rationale: Nothing in a conforming decoder refuses a file over an unknown host-OS byte - Info-ZIP's mapattr() simply falls through to its default branch - but the value is a finite enumeration and each member selects a different external-attribute interpretation, so it is Tier B.
VERECORD.HostOS.description: The host system that wrote the entry, which tells the decoder how to interpret ZIPDIRENTRY.deExternalAttributes.

evidence.note: APPNOTE 'Version Made By' upper byte host-system table lists exactly 0-19; the .bt's typedef enum <byte> HOSTOSTYPE at lines 44-65 enumerates the same 20 values.

VERECORD.HostOS.notes: Every member is a distinct branch in Info-ZIP mapattr() / Unix permission mapping (FAT/HPFS/NTFS/VFAT read DOS attribute bits, Unix/OSX read the POSIX mode in the high 16 bits, VMS/MVS read record formats), so emitting all 20 rather than a favourite is a real coverage win. Values 20-255 are unused by the specification and are not offered here because the .bt's enum type does not define them.

EXTRAFIELD.efHeaderID.tier_rationale: An unrecognised extra-field ID does not make a decoder refuse the file - the template's own switch falls to the default at line 277 and skips efDataSize bytes - so it fails the Tier A test, but the ID set is a finite enumeration and each recognised ID is a separate parse branch, which is Tier B.
EXTRAFIELD.efHeaderID.description: The extra-field tag that selects which substructure follows the 4-byte (ID, size) header.
EXTRAFIELD.efHeaderID.notes: All 44 members of the typedef enum <ushort> HEADERFLAG at lines 152-197 are listed in template order and none was dropped. The IDs the template gives a dedicated case are EH_Zip64 (line 233), EH_InfoZIPUnicodePath (line 239), EH_NTFS (line 245), EH_StrongEncryption (line 263) and EH_WzAES (line 271); every other member reaches the default branch and still exercises the size-driven skip, which is worth having.

EXTRAFIELD.efDataSize.tier_rationale: The extra-field walk advances by exactly this value (lines 410 and 505: 'len -= frExtraField.efDataSize + 4'), so a wrong value misaligns the file position and the next record's signature check at line 618/624 fails, at which point the template warns 'Unknown ZIP tag encountered' and returns -1 - no further bytes of the archive are parsed.
EXTRAFIELD.efDataSize.description: The number of data bytes in this extra field, immediately following its own 4-byte (efHeaderID, efDataSize) header.
EXTRAFIELD.efDataSize.covers: every byte of the case-specific substructure selected by EXTRAFIELD.efHeaderID at line 231, from the byte after efDataSize up to and including the last byte of efOriginalSize/efCompressedSize (EH_Zip64), efUnicodeName (EH_InfoZIPUnicodePath), the NTFS attribute list (EH_NTFS), Format..CertData (EH_StrongEncryption), deCompression (EH_WzAES) or efData (default)
EXTRAFIELD.efDataSize.notes: Never chosen independently: pick the extra field's contents first (they are free), then write their byte length here. Also note the EH_InfoZIPUnicodePath case computes its own data as efDataSize - 5 (line 243), so efDataSize must be at least 5 there, and EH_StrongEncryption subtracts 8 (line 269).

EXTRAFIELD.efOriginalSize.tier_rationale: This is the authoritative uncompressed size once ZIP64 is in play; a value that disagrees with the payload makes the decoder's post-inflate length check fail (Info-ZIP: 'incorrect length of compressed data', libzip: ZIP_ER_CRC / length mismatch) and the extracted entry is discarded.
EXTRAFIELD.efOriginalSize.description: The 64-bit original (uncompressed) size of the entry, present in the ZIP64 extra field when the true size does not fit in 32 bits.

evidence.note: APPNOTE ZIP64 Extended Information Extra Field (0x0001): Original Size is the uncompressed size and must equal the value the 32-bit field would hold; the 32-bit field is set to 0xFFFFFFFF to signal 'look here'.

EXTRAFIELD.efOriginalSize.covers: the decompressed content of ZIPFILERECORD.frData for the entry this extra field belongs to
EXTRAFIELD.efOriginalSize.notes: Compute it from the payload, never the reverse: choose the plaintext length freely, then write that length here and into frUncompressedSize / deUncompressedSize.

EXTRAFIELD.efCompressedSize.tier_rationale: The template uses this value as a hard seek at line 631 (FSkip(record.frExtraField.efCompressedSize)) whenever the local header declares 0xFFFFFFFF, so a wrong value leaves the file position off the next record boundary and the dispatcher aborts the parse with 'Unknown ZIP tag encountered'; real decoders fail the same way because they trust it to bound the inflate output.
EXTRAFIELD.efCompressedSize.description: The 64-bit compressed size of the entry's payload, present in the ZIP64 extra field when the true size does not fit in 32 bits.

evidence.note: APPNOTE ZIP64 Extended Information Extra Field (0x0001): Compressed Size is the size of the compressed data and must equal the on-disk byte count of the payload.

EXTRAFIELD.efCompressedSize.covers: the ZIPFILERECORD.frData byte run that follows the local header and its extra-field chain
EXTRAFIELD.efCompressedSize.notes: Derive it from the emitted compressed stream: build the deflate/stored payload first, measure it, then write the length here and into frCompressedSize / deCompressedSize.

EXTRAFIELD.efVersion.tier_rationale: Info-ZIP's process_UnicodeData() returns FALSE and discards the whole Unicode-path extra field when the version byte is not 1, so a wrong value stops the decoder from taking the Unicode-naming path at all - it never reaches the code that replaces the entry name.
EXTRAFIELD.efVersion.description: The revision byte of the Info-ZIP Unicode Path extra field (0x7075).

evidence.note: Info-ZIP ux-utf8 / APPNOTE Unicode Path Extra Field: 'Version: 1 byte, version of this extra field, currently 1'. The .bt declares the byte without comparing it, so the literal comes from the specification.

EXTRAFIELD.efVersion.notes: Emit 1. The template reads this byte in the 0x7075 branch (line 240) and Info-ZIP's process_UnicodeData() discards the whole Unicode-path field for any other value, reverting to ZIPFILERECORD.frFileName, so a wrong byte silently loses the field's effect instead of failing the archive.

EXTRAFIELD.efNameCRC32.tier_rationale: Info-ZIP recomputes the CRC-32 of the name stored in the local/central header and ignores the Unicode path field entirely when it does not match this value, so a wrong value makes the decoder skip the field and never enter its Unicode-naming branch.
EXTRAFIELD.efNameCRC32.description: The CRC-32 of the original (non-Unicode) file name bytes, used by decoders to confirm the Unicode path still belongs to this entry.

evidence.note: Info-ZIP Unicode Path Extra Field: 'NameCRC32: 4 bytes, CRC-32 checksum of the corresponding non-Unicode file name field'.

EXTRAFIELD.efNameCRC32.covers: the raw bytes of ZIPFILERECORD.frFileName (or ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileName in the central-directory copy), exactly frFileNameLength bytes with no NUL terminator
EXTRAFIELD.efNameCRC32.notes: Compute it from the name that was actually written; changing the name afterwards invalidates it.

EXTRAFIELD.efUnicodeName.tier_rationale: Once the version byte and NameCRC32 check out, decoders copy these bytes into the entry name verbatim without validating them, so pinning the text would remove a whole axis of path-handling diversity (deep directories, long names, non-ASCII names, trailing separators) for no depth.
EXTRAFIELD.efUnicodeName.description: The UTF-8 encoded file name carried by the Info-ZIP Unicode Path extra field.
EXTRAFIELD.efUnicodeName.notes: Its byte length is what EXTRAFIELD.efDataSize records (efDataSize - 5 = length after the 1-byte version and 4-byte CRC), so the length is derived from this free content rather than the other way round. The specification asks for UTF-8 without a NUL; decoders do not enforce it.

EXTRAFIELD.Reserved.tier_rationale: The NTFS extra field's four reserved bytes are stepped over without being read - the template advances straight to the attribute list at line 250 - and no mainstream decoder validates them, so fixing them to zero would buy nothing and would remove four free bytes per NTFS field.
EXTRAFIELD.Reserved.description: The reserved dword at the head of the NTFS extra field (0x000a) attribute list.

evidence.snippet: int Reserved;   //4 bytes    Reserved for future use

EXTRAFIELD.Reserved.notes: The comment says 'Reserved for future use', which is the classic sign of a field nobody checks; it is left free deliberately.

EXTRAFIELD.Tag.tier_rationale: A tag other than 0x0001 does not make a decoder refuse the file - the template simply takes the else branch at line 258 and reads the attribute as opaque bytes - but the specification defines exactly one tag, so the legal set is finite and belongs in Tier B.
EXTRAFIELD.Tag.description: The NTFS attribute tag identifying which attribute the following (Size, data) pair carries.

evidence.snippet: ushort Tag;        //2 bytes    NTFS attribute tag value #1
evidence.note: APPNOTE NTFS Extra Field (0x000a) defines a single attribute tag, 0x0001, whose data is three 8-byte Win32 FILETIME values.

EXTRAFIELD.Tag.notes: Line 252 compares it against the literal 0x001 to select the FILETIME triple; anything else falls through to 'byte Data[Size]'. Only one value exists, so this entry is effectively a pin, but it is recorded as an enumeration because that is what the specification defines.

EXTRAFIELD.Size.tier_rationale: The NTFS attribute walk advances by exactly this value (line 260: 'len -= Size + 4'), so a wrong value desynchronises the attribute list, corrupts EXTRAFIELD.efDataSize's accounting and pushes the following record off its signature boundary, where the dispatcher aborts.
EXTRAFIELD.Size.description: The byte length of one NTFS attribute's data, immediately following its own 4-byte (Tag, Size) header.

evidence.snippet: ushort Size;       //2 bytes    Size of attribute #1, in bytes
evidence.note: APPNOTE NTFS Extra Field: Size is the attribute data size in bytes; for tag 0x0001 it is 24 because the data is three 8-byte FILETIME values.

EXTRAFIELD.Size.covers: Mtime, Atime and Ctime when Tag is 0x0001 (24 bytes), otherwise the EXTRAFIELD.Data run read at line 259
EXTRAFIELD.Size.notes: For the timestamp attribute this is a fixed 24; for any other tag it is simply the length of whatever free bytes were emitted.

EXTRAFIELD.Mtime.tier_rationale: A Win32 FILETIME is copied into the entry's timestamp and never validated - Info-ZIP and libzip accept any 64-bit value including zero - so restricting it would remove free bytes and a diversity axis (timestamp conversion and DOS-time rounding paths) while buying no depth.
EXTRAFIELD.Mtime.description: The file last-modification time as a Win32 FILETIME (100 ns intervals since 1601-01-01 UTC).

evidence.snippet: FILETIME Mtime;      //8 bytes    File last modification time

EXTRAFIELD.Mtime.notes: The layout is informational only: no minimum, maximum or representative value is implied, and the field is deliberately left free.

EXTRAFIELD.Atime.tier_rationale: Like Mtime, the last-access FILETIME is stored and converted but never checked, so any value still yields an archive the decoder processes; constraining it would cost diversity for nothing.
EXTRAFIELD.Atime.description: The file last-access time as a Win32 FILETIME.

evidence.snippet: FILETIME Atime;      //8 bytes    File last access time

EXTRAFIELD.Atime.notes: Free value: draw any 8-byte Win32 FILETIME (100 ns ticks since 1601-01-01 UTC), independently of EXTRAFIELD.Mtime. Neither the template (line 255) nor Info-ZIP validates it; only EXTRAFIELD.Size decides whether it is read at all, so keep the two consistent.

EXTRAFIELD.Ctime.tier_rationale: Like Mtime, the creation FILETIME is stored and converted but never checked, so any value still yields an archive the decoder processes; constraining it would cost diversity for nothing.
EXTRAFIELD.Ctime.description: The file creation time as a Win32 FILETIME.

evidence.snippet: FILETIME Ctime;     //8 bytes    File creation time

EXTRAFIELD.Ctime.notes: Free value: any 8-byte Win32 FILETIME, read at line 256 and never checked. Its presence is governed by EXTRAFIELD.Size, which may carry the 0x0001 tag only when the block really holds Mtime, Atime and Ctime.

EXTRAFIELD.Data.tier_rationale: This is the else-branch catch-all for an NTFS attribute tag nobody recognises; the template reads Size raw bytes and never inspects them, so the content is free and only its length (EXTRAFIELD.Size) is pinned.
EXTRAFIELD.Data.description: Opaque attribute data for an NTFS extra-field tag other than 0x0001.
EXTRAFIELD.Data.notes: Asked the opaque-array question: nothing must be inside it, because no decoder interprets an unrecognised NTFS attribute.

EXTRAFIELD.Format.tier_rationale: The strong-encryption extra field's format word is undefined by the specification and unread by mainstream decoders, so a wrong value cannot make one refuse the file; pinning it would only remove free bytes.
EXTRAFIELD.Format.description: The format-definition word at the head of the Strong Encryption Header extra field (0x0017).

evidence.snippet: ushort  Format;    //2 bytes  Format definition for this record

EXTRAFIELD.Format.notes: Free value: APPNOTE leaves the strong-encryption format definition undefined and no mainstream decoder reads it, so any ushort is safe. It is part of the 0x0017 block whose total byte count EXTRAFIELD.efDataSize must still cover.

EXTRAFIELD.AlgID.tier_rationale: An unrecognised algorithm ID makes a decoder report 'unsupported encryption algorithm' for that entry only, not refuse the archive, and the file still parses - so it fails the Tier A test - but it is a finite enumeration in which every member selects a different key-length and cipher path, which is Tier B.
EXTRAFIELD.AlgID.description: The encryption algorithm identifier in the Strong Encryption Header extra field (0x0017).

evidence.snippet: ALGFLAG AlgID;     //2 bytes  Encryption algorithm identifier

EXTRAFIELD.AlgID.notes: All 12 members of the typedef enum <ushort> ALGFLAG at lines 199-212 are listed, including AlgID_Unknown (0xFFFF) and the pre-5.2 RC2 spelling, because each is a distinct branch in a decoder that supports certificate-based decryption.

EXTRAFIELD.Bitlen.tier_rationale: The specification gives no closed set of key bit lengths across all algorithms (RC2 and Blowfish are variable), so this could only be argued into Tier B; the tie-break rule says choose Tier C, and no mainstream decoder reads this word in preference to AlgID.
EXTRAFIELD.Bitlen.description: The bit length of the encryption key named by EXTRAFIELD.AlgID.

evidence.snippet: ushort  Bitlen;    //2 bytes  Bit length of encryption key

EXTRAFIELD.Bitlen.notes: Conventionally agrees with AlgID (128/192/256 for the AES IDs, 112/168 for 3DES), but that convention is not recorded as a constraint because it is not a rule a decoder enforces.

EXTRAFIELD.Flags.tier_rationale: A wrong processing-flag word does not make a decoder refuse the archive - it changes whether a password or a certificate is demanded for that entry - but the specification defines exactly three values, so this is a finite enumeration and belongs in Tier B.
EXTRAFIELD.Flags.description: The strong-encryption processing flags saying what kind of secret is needed to decrypt the entry.
EXTRAFIELD.Flags.notes: All three members of the typedef enum <ushort> PRCFLAG at lines 220-224 are listed; 0 is not a member and is not offered.

EXTRAFIELD.CertData.tier_rationale: Asked the opaque-array question: the specification says this is PKCS#7 certificate-decryption data, but no ZIP decoder that parses the archive structure validates it - decryption happens later and only in certificate-aware tools - so the bytes are free and only their length (via EXTRAFIELD.efDataSize - 8) is pinned.
EXTRAFIELD.CertData.description: The certificate decryption extra-field data of the Strong Encryption Header (0x0017).

evidence.snippet: byte    CertData[efDataSize - 8];  //TSize-8  Certificate decryption extra field data

EXTRAFIELD.CertData.notes: If a future decoder under test does X.509 parsing here, this entry becomes a Tier A payload_wellformedness for DER-encoded PKCS#7; on the evidence available it is free.

EXTRAFIELD.version.tier_rationale: A wrong AE version does not make a decoder refuse the archive - it changes whether the entry's CRC-32 is expected to be zero and which key schedule is used - and only two values exist, so this is a finite enumeration in Tier B.
EXTRAFIELD.version.description: The WinZip AES extra-field (0x9901) vendor version: AE-1 or AE-2.

evidence.snippet: ushort version;         //2 bytes   Integer version number specific to the zip vendor
evidence.note: WinZip AE extra field 0x9901: version 0x0001 = AE-1 (CRC-32 retained), 0x0002 = AE-2 (CRC-32 field must be zero).

EXTRAFIELD.version.notes: AE-2 is preferred for depth because it is what current WinZip writes and what minizip-ng expects, and because it drives the frCrc == 0 dependency; AE-1 is still emitted since it takes the CRC-verifying branch.

EXTRAFIELD.VendorID.tier_rationale: WinZip and minizip-ng reject an AE extra field whose vendor ID is not the two characters 'AE' and then refuse to decrypt the entry, so the decoder stops before doing any useful work on that entry - which is the Tier A test.
EXTRAFIELD.VendorID.description: The two-character vendor identifier of the WinZip AES extra field (0x9901).

evidence.note: WinZip AE extra field 0x9901: 'VendorID: 2-character vendor ID, must be "AE"'.

EXTRAFIELD.VendorID.notes: Stored as two ASCII bytes in file order (0x41 then 0x45); there is no endianness question for a char[2].

EXTRAFIELD.Strength.tier_rationale: An unrecognised strength byte does not make a decoder refuse the archive, but it does decide the salt length and the AES key size, and only three values are defined - a finite enumeration, so Tier B.
EXTRAFIELD.Strength.description: The WinZip AES encryption strength, which fixes the key size and therefore the salt length.

evidence.snippet: AESMODE Strength;       //1 bytes   Integer mode value indicating AES encryption strength

EXTRAFIELD.Strength.notes: All three members of the typedef enum <byte> AESMODE at lines 214-218 are listed. The template's own switch at lines 440-451 maps 1/2/3 to salt lengths 8/12/16 (see the ZIPFILERECORD.SaltValue dependency); the byte is emitted as one byte here even though the surrounding WzAES fields are 2-byte aligned, because that is how the .bt declares it.

EXTRAFIELD.deCompression.tier_rationale: A wrong value here does not make a decoder refuse the archive; it names the codec the AES-CTR ciphertext wraps, so the decoder picks the wrong inflater and fails later - and the legal set is the finite COMPTYPE enumeration, which is Tier B.
EXTRAFIELD.deCompression.description: The real compression method applied to the file data before WinZip AE encryption wrapped it.

evidence.snippet: COMPTYPE deCompression; //2 bytes The actual compression method used to compress the file
evidence.note: WinZip AE extra field 0x9901: the compression method field of the local/central header is set to 99 and the true method is carried here.

EXTRAFIELD.deCompression.notes: Same full COMPTYPE member set as ZIPFILERECORD.frCompression; no member was dropped. Method 99 nested inside 99 is legal per the enum and is kept for that reason even though real writers do not produce it.

EXTRAFIELD.efData.tier_rationale: This is the default branch of the extra-field switch: the template reads efDataSize raw bytes and never inspects them, so the content is entirely free and only its length is pinned. Constraining the bytes would remove the single cheapest source of extra-field diversity.
EXTRAFIELD.efData.description: Opaque data of any extra field whose ID has no dedicated case in the template's switch.
EXTRAFIELD.efData.notes: Asked the opaque-array question: for the 39 HEADERFLAG members without a dedicated case, and for IDs outside the enum entirely, nothing specific must be inside - although a few well-known ones have documented layouts worth mimicking for depth in decoders that parse them (0x5455 extended timestamp: 1 flag byte + 4-byte time_t values; 0x7875 Info-ZIP new Unix: version 1, UID/GID size+value pairs; 0x7855 Info-ZIP Unix: 2 x 4-byte time_t + 2 x 2-byte uid/gid).

EXTRA64FIELD.efHeaderID.tier_rationale: Exactly as for EXTRAFIELD.efHeaderID: an unrecognised ID falls to the default at line 308 and the field is skipped rather than rejected, so it is not Tier A, but the legal set is the finite HEADERFLAG enumeration and each recognised ID selects a different parse branch, which is Tier B.
EXTRA64FIELD.efHeaderID.description: The extra-field tag selecting the substructure in the ZIP64 variant of the extra-field reader.
EXTRA64FIELD.efHeaderID.notes: Same 44 HEADERFLAG members as EXTRAFIELD.efHeaderID - no member was dropped - but this reader only specialises EH_Zip64 (line 296) and EH_InfoZIPUnicodePath (line 302); EH_NTFS, EH_StrongEncryption and EH_WzAES all reach the default. IMPORTANT: the typedef is declared at line 313 but is never instantiated by the dispatcher - its only use, inside ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD's DataSect branch, is commented out at line 545 - so these entries describe a structure the template can reach only if that loop is re-enabled.

EXTRA64FIELD.efDataSize.tier_rationale: This reader derives every following array length from the value (efUnicodeName at line 306, efData at line 310), so a wrong value either over-reads past the end of the record or under-reads and desynchronises the walk, after which the dispatcher's signature test fails and it aborts with 'Unknown ZIP tag encountered'.
EXTRA64FIELD.efDataSize.description: The number of data bytes in this extra field, immediately following its own (efHeaderID, efDataSize) header.
EXTRA64FIELD.efDataSize.covers: efOriginalSize and efCompressedSize (EH_Zip64), efUnicodeName (EH_InfoZIPUnicodePath) or efData (default) - every byte from the one after efDataSize to the end of the field
EXTRA64FIELD.efDataSize.notes: Note the deliberate deviation from APPNOTE and from EXTRAFIELD.efDataSize: this reader declares the size as a 4-byte uint rather than a ushort, so the header is 6 bytes here, not 4. Emit what the template declares; the commented-out loop at lines 542-547 still subtracts efDataSize + 4, which is the residual bug that keeps the typedef unused.

EXTRA64FIELD.efOriginalSize.tier_rationale: Same reasoning as EXTRAFIELD.efOriginalSize: this is the authoritative uncompressed size in the ZIP64 path, and a value that disagrees with the payload makes the decoder's post-inflate length check fail so the entry is discarded.
EXTRA64FIELD.efOriginalSize.description: The 64-bit original (uncompressed) size of the entry, in the ZIP64 extra field as read by the 4-byte-size variant of the extra-field reader.

evidence.note: APPNOTE ZIP64 Extended Information Extra Field (0x0001): Original Size is the uncompressed size; the 32-bit header field is set to 0xFFFFFFFF to signal that the real value lives here.

EXTRA64FIELD.efOriginalSize.covers: the decompressed content of ZIPFILERECORD.frData for the entry this extra field belongs to
EXTRA64FIELD.efOriginalSize.notes: Compute from the payload; keep it equal to EXTRAFIELD.efOriginalSize wherever both readers could apply.

EXTRA64FIELD.efCompressedSize.tier_rationale: Same reasoning as EXTRAFIELD.efCompressedSize: the template treats this as a hard seek distance (line 631) and decoders use it to bound the inflate output, so a wrong value ends the parse.
EXTRA64FIELD.efCompressedSize.description: The 64-bit compressed size of the entry's payload, in the ZIP64 extra field as read by the 4-byte-size variant of the extra-field reader.

evidence.note: APPNOTE ZIP64 Extended Information Extra Field (0x0001): Compressed Size is the on-disk byte count of the payload.

EXTRA64FIELD.efCompressedSize.covers: the ZIPFILERECORD.frData byte run that follows the local header and its extra-field chain
EXTRA64FIELD.efCompressedSize.notes: Derive from the emitted compressed stream, then mirror the value into frCompressedSize / deCompressedSize.

EXTRA64FIELD.efVersion.tier_rationale: Identical to EXTRAFIELD.efVersion: Info-ZIP discards the whole Unicode-path field when the version byte is not 1, so the decoder never reaches its Unicode-naming branch.
EXTRA64FIELD.efVersion.description: The revision byte of the Info-ZIP Unicode Path extra field (0x7075) as read by the 4-byte-size variant.

evidence.note: Info-ZIP Unicode Path Extra Field: 'Version: 1 byte, version of this extra field, currently 1'. The .bt declares the byte without comparing it, so the literal comes from the specification.

EXTRA64FIELD.efVersion.notes: Emit 1, exactly as for EXTRAFIELD.efVersion. Inert for this template: EXTRA64FIELD is declared at lines 289-313 but its only instantiation site is commented out at lines 542-547, so this entry documents the declaration rather than a byte a generator should emit.

EXTRA64FIELD.efNameCRC32.tier_rationale: Identical to EXTRAFIELD.efNameCRC32: Info-ZIP recomputes the CRC-32 of the header's name bytes and skips the Unicode path field on mismatch, so the field's effect is lost.
EXTRA64FIELD.efNameCRC32.description: The CRC-32 of the original (non-Unicode) file name bytes, in the Unicode Path extra field as read by the 4-byte-size variant.

evidence.note: Info-ZIP Unicode Path Extra Field: 'NameCRC32: 4 bytes, CRC-32 checksum of the corresponding non-Unicode file name field'.

EXTRA64FIELD.efNameCRC32.covers: the raw bytes of ZIPFILERECORD.frFileName (or ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileName), exactly frFileNameLength bytes with no NUL terminator
EXTRA64FIELD.efNameCRC32.notes: Compute from the name actually written.

EXTRA64FIELD.efUnicodeName.tier_rationale: Same as EXTRAFIELD.efUnicodeName: once the version byte and NameCRC32 are right the decoder copies these bytes into the entry name verbatim, so pinning the text would delete a diversity axis (long, deep, non-ASCII paths) without adding depth.
EXTRA64FIELD.efUnicodeName.description: The UTF-8 encoded file name carried by the Unicode Path extra field, as read by the 4-byte-size variant.
EXTRA64FIELD.efUnicodeName.notes: The subtraction of 5 assumes the 1-byte version plus 4-byte CRC precede it, i.e. the same convention as EXTRAFIELD; because efDataSize is 4 bytes wide in this reader the -5 is only consistent with the APPNOTE layout, not with the reader's own header width.

EXTRA64FIELD.efData.tier_rationale: Default branch of this reader's switch: the bytes are consumed by length only and never inspected, so their content is free and only efDataSize is pinned.
EXTRA64FIELD.efData.description: Opaque data of any extra field this reader has no dedicated case for.
EXTRA64FIELD.efData.notes: Asked the opaque-array question: nothing specific must be inside, because the reader never looks. Same guidance as EXTRAFIELD.efData applies if a decoder under test does parse well-known IDs (0x5455, 0x7875, 0x7855).

ZIPDATADESCR.ddSignature.tier_rationale: The template locates a streamed entry's descriptor by scanning forward for exactly this dword (line 468: FindFirst(S_ZIPDATADESCR,...)) and the top-level dispatcher also matches it (line 634); if it is absent or wrong the descriptor is never found, the parse desynchronises and the dispatcher aborts at line 666 - so the archive is refused.
ZIPDATADESCR.ddSignature.description: The 4-byte signature that begins an optional data descriptor (0x08074b50).

evidence.note: APPNOTE: the data descriptor signature 0x08074b50 is 'currently not used by many zip implementations' but PKWARE requires it when present; the .bt hard-codes the literal in the SignatureTYPE enum at line 36 and compares it at lines 468 and 634.

lookahead.note: The descriptor is located by forward search for its 4-byte signature rather than by reading a fixed-width field, because bit 3 of the flags means the payload length was unknown when the local header was written. The searched-for literal S_ZIPDATADESCR is 0x08074b50 (enum line 36); the distance found, posNext - posCurrent, becomes the length of frData at line 471.

ZIPDATADESCR.ddSignature.notes: Emit 0x08074B50 whenever a data descriptor is present. APPNOTE treats the signature as optional, but this template finds a streamed entry's descriptor by scanning forward for exactly this dword (line 468) and dispatches on it as a record tag (line 634), so a descriptor without it is invisible and the streamed sizes are never read.

ZIPDATADESCR.ddCRC.tier_rationale: This is the CRC the decoder compares against the payload it just inflated for a streamed entry; a mismatch makes Info-ZIP report 'incorrect data CRC-32' and libzip return ZIP_ER_CRC, so the entry is rejected before any further work.
ZIPDATADESCR.ddCRC.description: The CRC-32 of the uncompressed file data, supplied after the payload because it was unknown when the local header was written.

evidence.note: APPNOTE data descriptor: crc-32 of the uncompressed file data; it must equal the CRC of the bytes the payload expands to.

ZIPDATADESCR.ddCRC.covers: the uncompressed expansion of the entry's payload - for COMP_STORED the frData bytes themselves, for COMP_DEFLATE the inflated output
ZIPDATADESCR.ddCRC.notes: Must equal ZIPFILERECORD.frCrc, which is written as 0 in the local header when bit 3 of the flags is set. Compute once from the plaintext and write it in both places.

ZIPDATADESCR.ddCompressedSize.tier_rationale: For a streamed entry this is the only place the compressed length is recorded, and the decoder uses it to know where the payload ends; a wrong value makes the next record start at the wrong offset, the dispatcher's ReadUInt test at line 618/624 fails and it aborts with 'Unknown ZIP tag encountered' - the archive is refused.
ZIPDATADESCR.ddCompressedSize.description: The size in bytes of the compressed payload, supplied after the data because it was unknown when the local header was written.

evidence.note: APPNOTE data descriptor: compressed size of the file data; must equal the on-disk byte count of the payload.

ZIPDATADESCR.ddCompressedSize.covers: the ZIPFILERECORD.frData run that immediately precedes this descriptor
ZIPDATADESCR.ddCompressedSize.notes: Must equal ZIPFILERECORD.frCompressedSize, which is written as 0 in the local header when bit 3 of the flags is set (that zero is exactly what makes the template take the FindFirst path at line 462-471).

ZIPDATADESCR.ddUncompressedSize.tier_rationale: This is the length the decoder checks the inflate output against for a streamed entry; a mismatch makes Info-ZIP report 'incorrect length of compressed data' and libzip return ZIP_ER_INVAL, so the entry is rejected before it is handed back.
ZIPDATADESCR.ddUncompressedSize.description: The size in bytes of the uncompressed file data, supplied after the data because it was unknown when the local header was written.

evidence.note: APPNOTE data descriptor: uncompressed size of the file data.

ZIPDATADESCR.ddUncompressedSize.covers: the uncompressed expansion of the entry's payload - the frData bytes themselves for COMP_STORED, the inflated output for COMP_DEFLATE
ZIPDATADESCR.ddUncompressedSize.notes: Must equal ZIPFILERECORD.frUncompressedSize, which is written as 0 in the local header when bit 3 of the flags is set.

ZIPFILERECORD.frSignature.tier_rationale: The top-level dispatcher reads the dword at the current offset (line 618) and compares it against S_ZIPFILERECORD (line 624); any other value falls to the else at line 664, warns 'Unknown ZIP tag encountered. Template stopped.' and returns -1, so the rest of the archive is never parsed. Real decoders reject the file the same way because the local header signature is how they find each entry.
ZIPFILERECORD.frSignature.description: The 4-byte signature that begins a local file header (0x04034b50).

evidence.note: APPNOTE local file header: signature = 0x04034b50; the .bt declares the literal in the SignatureTYPE enum at line 35.

lookahead.note: The dispatcher mines its known-good value set from this single call site and compares it against all seven SignatureTYPE members (lines 624-659): 0x04034b50 local file header, 0x08074b50 data descriptor, 0x02014b50 central directory entry, 0x05054b50 digital signature, 0x06064b50 ZIP64 end-of-central-directory record, 0x07064b50 ZIP64 end-of-central-directory locator, 0x06054b50 end-of-central-directory locator. Anything else hits the else at line 664: Warning + return -1.

ZIPFILERECORD.frSignature.notes: Emit 0x04034B50 at the start of every local header. The dispatcher reads the dword at the current offset (line 618), matches S_ZIPFILERECORD at line 624 and aborts the whole parse at line 664 on anything else; ZIPDIRENTRY.deHeaderOffset must point at this byte.

ZIPFILERECORD.frVersion.tier_rationale: Covered by the shared VERECORD.Version entry: a wrong version byte produces at most a warning in Info-ZIP and the archive still opens, so it is not Tier A, but its legal set is the finite APPNOTE version table, which is Tier B.
ZIPFILERECORD.frVersion.description: The version-needed-to-extract word of the local file header: version byte plus host-system byte.
ZIPFILERECORD.frVersion.notes: The version byte is the low byte of the 2-byte VERECORD; the high byte is VERECORD.HostOS. Same legal set as the shared entry - no member dropped - but here the value must be at least the level implied by the entry's own features (45 when a ZIP64 extra field is present, 51 for WinZip AE, 46 for bzip2, 63 for LZMA/PPMd).

ZIPFILERECORD.frFlags.tier_rationale: A wrong flag word does not make a conforming decoder refuse the archive - it changes which decryption, streaming and naming path that one entry takes, and the file still opens - so it fails the Tier A test; it is a finite bitmask whose 16 named bits are all defined by the specification, which is Tier B.
ZIPFILERECORD.frFlags.description: The general purpose bit flag of the local file header: 16 independent bits selecting encryption, streaming, UTF-8 naming and compression sub-modes.

evidence.note: APPNOTE general purpose bit flag: bits 0, 3, 6, 11, 13 are defined as encrypted / data descriptor / strong encryption / UTF-8 names / central-directory encryption; bits 1-2 and 4-5 are compression-method options; the rest are reserved by PKWARE.

ZIPFILERECORD.frFlags.completeness_reason: The legal set is every OR-combination of the 16 valid_bits, i.e. all 65536 values 0-65535; no bit is reserved-should-be-zero and no combination is illegal. The listed values are 0, each of the 16 single bits, and the four combinations the template's own conditionals actually test at lines 415, 435 and 462. Listing all 65536 would be noise; nothing outside the list is excluded.
ZIPFILERECORD.frFlags.notes: All 16 members of the typedef enum <ushort> FLAGTYPE at lines 112-130 are recorded as valid_bits and none was dropped, including the eight PKWARE-reserved and currently-unused bits, because the template's display function read_FLAGTYPE (lines 132-150) walks the value one bit at a time (its loop at line 138 stops just below 0x8000, so it prints 15 of the 16 names; the sixteenth bit is still legal in a file). The bits that drive control flow are 0x0008 (selects the ZIPDATADESCR path and zeroed size/CRC fields), 0x0001 together with 0x0040 (selects StrongEncryptedHeader), 0x0001 together with frCompression 99 (selects the WinZip AE path), and 0x0800 (names and comments are UTF-8).

ZIPFILERECORD.frCompression.tier_rationale: An unsupported method makes a decoder report 'unsupported compression method' for that entry, but the archive still opens and the other entries are still processed, so it is not Tier A; the legal set is the finite COMPTYPE enumeration and each member selects a different decompression branch, which is exactly Tier B.
ZIPFILERECORD.frCompression.description: The compression method applied to the entry's payload, and therefore the codec ZIPFILERECORD.frData must be a valid stream of.

evidence.note: APPNOTE compression method table: 0 stored, 1 shrunk, 2-5 reduced 1-4, 6 imploded, 7 reserved for Tokenizing, 8 deflated, 9 Deflate64, 10 PKWARE imploding, 12 bzip2, 14 LZMA, 18 IBM terse, 19 IBM LZ77 z, 96 JPEG, 97 WavPack, 98 PPMd, 99 WinZip AE encryption.

ZIPFILERECORD.frCompression.notes: All 19 members of the typedef enum <short> COMPTYPE at lines 88-110 are listed in template order and none was dropped, including COMP_TOKEN (7) which the specification only reserves and COMP_WzAES (99) which is not a codec but a marker that the real method lives in EXTRAFIELD.deCompression. 11, 13, 15-17 and 20-95 are gaps in the enum and are not offered. This field is the selector for ZIPFILERECORD.frData's payload_wellformedness.

ZIPFILERECORD.frFileTime.tier_rationale: Timestamps are named Tier C outright: the MS-DOS time word is converted and stored, never validated, and any value - including an out-of-range seconds field - still yields an archive every decoder processes, so constraining it would cost diversity (the rounding and clamping paths) for no depth.
ZIPFILERECORD.frFileTime.description: The entry's last-modification time as an MS-DOS time word (bits 15-11 hours, 10-5 minutes, 4-0 seconds/2).
ZIPFILERECORD.frFileTime.notes: Layout is informational only. No minimum, maximum or representative value is implied; the field is deliberately left free, and it must stay equal to ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileTime for the same entry only if the generator wants the two headers to agree - decoders read the central directory copy.

ZIPFILERECORD.frFileDate.tier_rationale: Timestamps are named Tier C outright: the MS-DOS date word is converted and stored, never validated, and any value still yields an archive every decoder processes, so constraining it would cost diversity (date-conversion and pre-1980 clamping paths) for no depth.
ZIPFILERECORD.frFileDate.description: The entry's last-modification date as an MS-DOS date word (bits 15-9 year since 1980, 8-5 month, 4-0 day).
ZIPFILERECORD.frFileDate.notes: Layout is informational only; the field is deliberately left free, including month/day values no real calendar produces, because Info-ZIP and libzip clamp rather than reject.

ZIPFILERECORD.frCrc.tier_rationale: This is the value every decoder compares against the CRC it computes while inflating; a mismatch makes Info-ZIP report 'incorrect data CRC-32' and libzip return ZIP_ER_CRC, so the entry is rejected and never handed to the caller - the decoder stops before doing useful work with the data.
ZIPFILERECORD.frCrc.description: The CRC-32 of the entry's uncompressed file data, as recorded in the local file header.

evidence.note: APPNOTE local file header: crc-32 of the uncompressed file data; when bit 3 of the flags is set this field is written as 0 and the real value follows the payload in the data descriptor.

ZIPFILERECORD.frCrc.covers: the uncompressed expansion of ZIPFILERECORD.frData - the frData bytes themselves for COMP_STORED, the inflated output for COMP_DEFLATE, the AES-decrypted-then-inflated output for COMP_WzAES
ZIPFILERECORD.frCrc.notes: Compute it from the plaintext before compressing. Two exceptions: when frFlags bit 3 is set the local-header copy is 0 and ZIPDATADESCR.ddCRC carries the real value; when the entry is WinZip AE-2 (EXTRAFIELD.version == 2) the specification requires this field to be 0 even in the central directory.

ZIPFILERECORD.frCompressedSize.tier_rationale: The template uses this value as the literal length of every payload branch it reads (lines 433, 455, 460), and the top-level loop resumes at whatever offset that leaves, so a wrong value ends the record at the wrong place, the next ReadUInt at line 618 misses every signature and the template aborts with 'Unknown ZIP tag encountered. Template stopped.'; real decoders fail identically because it bounds the inflate input.
ZIPFILERECORD.frCompressedSize.description: The size in bytes of the entry's compressed payload as it appears in the file.

evidence.note: APPNOTE local file header: compressed size, the exact byte count of the file data that follows the header, extra fields and name.

ZIPFILERECORD.frCompressedSize.covers: the whole ZIPFILERECORD.frData run plus, when the entry is encrypted, the SaltValue, PassVerification and AuthenticationCode bytes and the StrongEncryptedHeader - i.e. every byte between the end of the extra-field chain and the start of the next record (or the data descriptor)
ZIPFILERECORD.frCompressedSize.notes: Derive it from the bytes actually emitted, never the reverse. Write 0 here when frFlags bit 3 is set (that zero is what makes the template take the FindFirst path at line 462); write 0xFFFFFFFF here when the true size does not fit in 32 bits and EXTRAFIELD.efCompressedSize carries it.

ZIPFILERECORD.frUncompressedSize.tier_rationale: Decoders size their output buffer from this field and, for COMP_STORED, use it as the exact payload length; a wrong value makes the extracted data fail the length check the decoder applies before handing it to the caller, so the entry is refused rather than merely annotated.
ZIPFILERECORD.frUncompressedSize.description: The size in bytes of the entry's file data after decompression.

evidence.note: APPNOTE local file header: uncompressed size of the file data; for COMP_STORED it equals compressed size, for a deflated entry it is the inflate output length.

ZIPFILERECORD.frUncompressedSize.covers: the decompressed expansion of ZIPFILERECORD.frData; for COMP_STORED the two sizes are identical, for COMP_WzAES it excludes the SaltValue, PassVerification and AuthenticationCode overhead that inflates compressed size
ZIPFILERECORD.frUncompressedSize.notes: Derive it from the plaintext the generator chose; never shrink the plaintext to fit a value picked first. Write 0 here when frFlags bit 3 is set and ZIPDATADESCR.ddUncompressedSize carries the real value; write 0xFFFFFFFF here when the true size does not fit in 32 bits and EXTRAFIELD.efOriginalSize carries it.

ZIPFILERECORD.frFileNameLength.tier_rationale: It is a length the template uses directly as an array size (line 404, 'char frFileName[frFileNameLength]'), so a wrong value desynchronises every byte after it; the decoder then reads the extra field from inside the name and no subsequent signature matches, which is a refusal rather than a warning.
ZIPFILERECORD.frFileNameLength.description: The number of bytes in this header's file-name field.

evidence.note: APPNOTE local file header: file name length, the byte count of the name that follows the extra-field length field.

ZIPFILERECORD.frFileNameLength.notes: The count is in bytes, not characters: a UTF-8 name with non-ASCII characters (frFlags bit 11 set) contributes 2-4 bytes per code point, and a directory entry's trailing '/' counts. Must not exceed 65535 because the field is 16 bits.

ZIPFILERECORD.frExtraFieldLength.tier_rationale: It is the exact byte budget of the extra-field chain the template then walks field by field (lines 419-421), so a wrong value makes each EXTRAFIELD chain read garbage IDs and lengths and lands the payload at the wrong offset - a structural failure, not a cosmetic one.
ZIPFILERECORD.frExtraFieldLength.description: The total number of bytes occupied by the chain of extra fields that follows the file name.

evidence.note: APPNOTE local file header: extra field length, the byte count of the concatenated 4-byte-header extra fields that follow the file name.

ZIPFILERECORD.frExtraFieldLength.covers: the whole EXTRAFIELD chain the while loop at lines 407-411 walks, i.e. the sum over its members of 2 (efHeaderID) + 2 (efDataSize) + efDataSize
ZIPFILERECORD.frExtraFieldLength.notes: Must equal the sum of 4 + efDataSize over every chain member and must not exceed 65535. The local-header chain and the central-directory chain are separate budgets: the specification allows them to differ (a ZIP64 field is often only in the central directory), so this value is not simply copied from deExtraFieldLength.

ZIPFILERECORD.frFileName.tier_rationale: Text is named Tier C outright: the name is stored and compared against nothing, and any byte sequence of the declared length still yields an archive the decoder opens, so constraining it would remove the path-traversal, backslash and non-UTF-8 branches that decoders handle specially.
ZIPFILERECORD.frFileName.description: The entry's path name as raw bytes, with '/' as the directory separator.
ZIPFILERECORD.frFileName.notes: Only its byte length is constrained (by ZIPFILERECORD.frFileNameLength); the content is free. A directory entry's name ends with '/' and carries a zero-length payload. When frFlags bit 11 is set the bytes are UTF-8, otherwise CP437 per the specification; both are legal and both should be generated.

ZIPFILERECORD.frExtraField.tier_rationale: How many extra fields an entry carries is a repetition count: any number from zero upward is legal, unknown IDs are ignored by every conforming decoder, and a wrong count costs nothing because the chain is bounded by frExtraFieldLength - so the count stays Tier C while the total byte budget it fills is Tier A.
ZIPFILERECORD.frExtraField.description: The chain of optional extra fields between the file name and the compressed payload of a local file header.

evidence.note: APPNOTE: the extra field is a sequence of variable-length records, each a 2-byte header ID, a 2-byte data size and that many data bytes; a decoder must skip records whose ID it does not recognise.

ZIPFILERECORD.frExtraField.notes: Leave the number of records free (0, 1, or many) - it is a genuine diversity axis, and the ZIP64, Unicode Path, NTFS and WinZip-AE readers are four distinct code paths that only run when the corresponding record is present. The one hard rule is the loop's exact termination: local len starts at frExtraFieldLength and subtracts efDataSize + 4 per record (line 410), so the record sizes must sum exactly to frExtraFieldLength. The same field name is used at line 438 to reach back into the last record read, which is why the template can consult frExtraField.efHeaderID and frExtraField.Strength after the loop.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.IVSi.tier_rationale: It is used directly as an array size (line 420, 'byte IVData[IVSize]') and subtracted from the payload length at line 433, so a wrong value both desynchronises the record and produces a negative or oversized frData length - the parse aborts rather than continuing.
ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.IVSi.description: The number of bytes of initialisation vector that follow this field in the strong-encryption header.

evidence.note: APPNOTE strong-encryption header: format 2 (0x0002) records 'ivSize' as the length in bytes of the encryption initialization vector, immediately followed by ivData of that many bytes.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.IVSi.notes: Only reached when frFlags has both bit 0 and bit 6 set (line 415). Must equal the byte length of the IV the generator emits, and the whole header plus payload must still sum to frCompressedSize - 6 as line 433 assumes.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.IVDa.tier_rationale: The initialisation vector's contents are opaque to the parser: the template reads IVSize bytes and inspects none of them, and a decoder without the passphrase never uses them, so any byte sequence of the declared length is equally acceptable and only its length (IVSize) is pinned.

evidence.note: APPNOTE strong-encryption header: ivData, the initialization vector used to seed the cipher; its length is given by ivSize.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.IVDa.notes: Asked-and-answered opaque array: nothing structured is required inside it. Leave the bytes free; the length is derived from ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.IVSize.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.Size.tier_rationale: Line 433 subtracts it from frCompressedSize to size the payload, so a wrong value makes frData the wrong length and the following record signature is read from the middle of the data - the dispatcher then aborts. It is also a length field, which is Tier A by definition.
ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.Size.description: The size in bytes of the remaining strong-encryption header after the initialisation vector (the block that starts at Format and ends at VCRC32).

evidence.note: APPNOTE strong-encryption header: 'Size' is the size of the rest of the header, i.e. the number of bytes from the format field through the end of the certificate / validation data block.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.Size.covers: the fixed fields Format, AlgID, BitLen, Flags, ErdSize, Reserved, VSize, VCRC32 plus the ErdData and VData variable runs - i.e. every byte from the Format field to the end of the header
ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.Size.notes: Confidence is medium because the .bt gives no arithmetic tying Size to the fields it precedes; the APPNOTE layout implies Size = 2 (Format) + 2 (AlgID) + 2 (BitLen) + 2 (Flags) + 2 (ErdSize) + ErdSize + 4 (Reserved) + 2 (VSize) + VData + 4 (VCRC32). Only reached when frFlags has both bit 0 and bit 6 set.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.Form.tier_rationale: The template reads the word and never compares it, and no mainstream decoder validates the in-header format word either - it identifies the cipher from AlgID instead - so a wrong value cannot make one refuse the file; pinning it would only remove free bytes.
ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.Form.description: The format-definition word at the head of the in-header strong-encryption block (the same layout the 0x0017 extra field carries, recorded as EXTRAFIELD.Format there).

evidence.note: APPNOTE strong-encryption header: 'Format, format definition for this record'; the published specification defines no closed set of values for it, and 0x0002 is the only one in general use.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.Form.notes: Treated exactly like EXTRAFIELD.Format. Only reached when frFlags has both bit 0 and bit 6 set.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.AlgI.tier_rationale: An unrecognised algorithm identifier makes a certificate-aware decoder report 'unsupported encryption algorithm' for that entry only, so it fails the Tier A test, but the legal set is the finite ALGFLAG enumeration and each member selects a different cipher and key-length path - Tier B.
ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.AlgI.description: The encryption algorithm identifier of the in-header strong-encryption block.

evidence.note: APPNOTE strong-encryption header: 'AlgID, encryption algorithm identifier', the same 12-value table as the 0x0017 extra field.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.AlgI.notes: The identical legal set recorded on EXTRAFIELD.AlgID; all 12 members of the typedef enum <ushort> ALGFLAG at lines 199-212 are listed and none dropped. Note that AlgID_Unknown (0xFFFF) is a legal on-disk value that the specification uses to mean 'the algorithm is not identified here', so it must stay in the set.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.BitL.tier_rationale: No closed set of key bit lengths exists across all the algorithms AlgID can name (RC2, Blowfish and Twofish are variable-length), so this could only be argued into Tier B, and the tie-break rule says choose Tier C; the template reads the word and never checks it.
ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.BitL.description: The bit length of the encryption key named by ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.AlgID.

evidence.note: APPNOTE strong-encryption header: 'Bitlen, bit length of encryption key'.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.BitL.notes: Spelled BitLen here and Bitlen in the EXTRAFIELD block - both spellings are recorded because the schema requires the identifiers as written in the .bt. Conventionally agrees with AlgID (128/192/256 for the AES IDs, 112/168 for 3DES) but no decoder enforces that, so it is not recorded as a constraint.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.Flag.tier_rationale: A wrong processing-flag word does not make a decoder refuse the archive - it changes whether a password or a certificate is demanded for that entry - but the specification defines exactly three values, so it is a finite enumeration and belongs in Tier B.
ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.Flag.description: The strong-encryption processing flags of the in-header block, saying what kind of secret is needed to decrypt the entry.

evidence.note: APPNOTE strong-encryption header: 'Flags, processing flags' - password required, certificates only, or password or certificate.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.Flag.notes: The identical legal set recorded on EXTRAFIELD.Flags; all three members of the typedef enum <ushort> PRCFLAG at lines 220-224 are listed and 0 is not a member so it is not offered. Declared as a bare ushort at line 425 rather than as PRCFLAG, but it occupies the same slot the extra field types as PRCFLAG.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.ErdS.tier_rationale: It is a length used directly as an array size (line 427, 'byte ErdData[ErdSize]') inside a block whose total size the payload arithmetic at line 433 depends on, so a wrong value desynchronises the record and every following signature - a refusal, not a warning.
ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.ErdS.description: The number of bytes of encryption-recipient (certificate) data that follow this field.

evidence.note: APPNOTE strong-encryption header: 'ErdSize' followed by 'ErdData' of that many bytes - the encryption recipient data list, present when the certificate-only processing flag is used.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.ErdS.notes: Zero is legal and normal for password-based strong encryption (Flags = pfPassword), in which case ErdData is an empty run.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.ErdD.tier_rationale: Asked the opaque-array question: the specification says this holds the encryption-recipient certificate list, but structure-parsing decoders read the byte run and never interpret it, and only a certificate-aware decrypter with the private key could validate it - so the bytes are free and only their length (ErdSize) is pinned.
ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.ErdD.description: The encryption-recipient data of the in-header strong-encryption block.

evidence.note: APPNOTE strong-encryption header: encryption recipient data (certificate list).

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.ErdD.notes: If a future decoder under test parses X.509/PKCS#7 here, this entry becomes a Tier A payload_wellformedness for DER-encoded recipient data; on the evidence available it is free.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.Rese.tier_rationale: Reserved-for-future-use fields that nobody checks are Tier C by the prompt's own rule: the template reads the word at line 428 and compares it against nothing, and no decoder refuses an archive over it, so writing a non-zero value costs no depth.
ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.Rese.description: The reserved word in the in-header strong-encryption block, between the recipient data and the validation block.
ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.Rese.notes: Deliberately not pinned to 0. The same word is zero-checked in some PKWARE tooling but neither this template nor the mainstream decoders reject a non-zero value.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.VSiz.tier_rationale: It is used directly as an array size, and the template subtracts 4 from it (line 430, 'byte VData[VSize - 4]'), so a value below 4 produces a negative length and any other wrong value desynchronises the record and breaks the payload arithmetic at line 433.
ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.VSiz.description: The total size in bytes of the validation block, counted from this field's follower through the trailing VCRC32 (which is why the template subtracts 4).

evidence.note: APPNOTE strong-encryption header: 'VSize' is the size of the validation data block; the last 4 bytes of it are the validation CRC-32.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.VSiz.notes: Must be at least 4 so that VSize - 4 is a valid array length, and must equal 4 + the byte length of VData. Confidence is medium because the .bt's own arithmetic (VSize - 4) is the only evidence for what the count includes.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.VDat.tier_rationale: Asked the opaque-array question: the specification calls this the validation data used to check a derived key during decryption, but no structure parser interprets it - it is consumed only by a decrypter that already holds the secret - so the bytes are free and only their length (VSize - 4) is pinned.
ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.VDat.description: The validation data of the in-header strong-encryption block, excluding the trailing 4-byte validation CRC.

evidence.note: APPNOTE strong-encryption header: validation data, used to verify that the correct key was derived.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.VDat.notes: Left free deliberately. The generator should emit VSize - 4 random or zero bytes rather than trying to produce cryptographically valid validation data, which would require the passphrase.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.VCRC.tier_rationale: It is a checksum, which the tier definitions place in Tier A: a decrypting decoder compares it against the CRC of the data it recovered and rejects the entry on mismatch, so a wrong value stops the decoder before it does useful work with the plaintext.
ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.VCRC.description: The validation CRC-32 at the end of the strong-encryption validation block.

evidence.note: APPNOTE strong-encryption header: 'VCRC32', the CRC-32 of the validation data block, used to confirm key derivation.

ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.VCRC.covers: the validation data block that precedes it, i.e. ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.VData
ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader.VCRC.notes: Reachable only on the frFlags bit 0 + bit 6 path. Confidence is medium: the .bt names the field VCRC32 but never computes it, and the specification describes it as a CRC over the validation data rather than over the plaintext, which is what ZIPFILERECORD.frCrc covers. A generator without the passphrase cannot make this check pass end-to-end, so it must at least be computed over the VData it actually emitted.

ZIPFILERECORD.frData.tier_rationale: This is the format's compressed payload and the highest-value entry in the file: it is declared as an opaque byte run (uchar frData[frCompressedSize], line 460) that says nothing about its contents, yet a decoder that reaches it immediately hands it to an inflate/bzip2/LZMA routine, and a malformed stream makes it report 'invalid compressed data' and stop before doing any useful work - exactly the PNG IDAT case that gained 8.2 points.
ZIPFILERECORD.frData.description: The entry's compressed file data, in the codec selected by ZIPFILERECORD.frCompression, spanning frCompressedSize bytes.

evidence.note: APPNOTE: file data is compressed with the method named in the compression method field; for method 8 the data is a raw DEFLATE stream per RFC 1951 with no zlib header and no Adler-32 trailer.

ZIPFILERECORD.frData.codec: selected by ZIPFILERECORD.frCompression - see codec_by_value for all 19 methods. The two a generator can always emit are 0 (stored: no codec at all) and 8 (raw DEFLATE per RFC 1951, with no zlib 0x78 header and no Adler-32 trailer).
ZIPFILERECORD.frData.must_produce: frCompressedSize bytes that form one complete, self-terminating stream in the selected codec and that decompress to exactly frUncompressedSize bytes whose CRC-32 equals frCrc. On the WinZip AES path the same byte range is wrapped as SaltValue[lenSalt] + PassVerification[2] + ciphertext + AuthenticationCode[10], so frCompressedSize counts the envelope, not the plaintext. On the strong-encryption path it counts IVSize + Size + 6 + ErdSize + payload.
ZIPFILERECORD.frData.decoder_gate: Late and per-entry, which is what makes it valuable: Info-ZIP unzip lists the archive fine, then reports 'invalid compressed data--format killed' or 'incorrect length of compressed data' for that one entry and extracts nothing; Python zipfile raises zlib.error ('invalid block type', 'invalid distance too far back', 'invalid stored block lengths') from read() after namelist() succeeded; libzip returns ZIP_ER_ZLIB / ZIP_ER_INCONS from zip_fread. A decoder therefore reaches the local header, the extra-field chain, the whole central directory and the EOCD before it touches these bytes.
ZIPFILERECORD.frData.generation_strategy: Choose the plaintext first and the method second, then measure. Stored (0): copy the plaintext verbatim, set frUncompressedSize == frCompressedSize == its byte length and frCrc == CRC-32 of those bytes. Deflate (8): compress with a raw-mode deflate (Python zlib.compressobj(level, zlib.DEFLATED, -15); zlib deflateInit2 with windowBits -15), set frCompressedSize to the length of the compressed output, frUncompressedSize to the plaintext length, frCrc to CRC-32 of the plaintext. Verify by decompressing with zlib.decompressobj(-15) and comparing lengths before writing anything. The cheapest always-correct construction is method 0, whose 'stream' is the plaintext itself; a single raw deflate stored block gives the same bytes under method 8.

0.requirement: The bytes ARE the plaintext: emit them verbatim, set frUncompressedSize == frCompressedSize == the plaintext length, and frCrc == CRC-32 of those bytes.

8.requirement: A complete DEFLATE bit stream: the last block must have BFINAL=1, every block must declare a valid BTYPE (00 stored, 01 fixed Huffman, 10 dynamic Huffman) and end with an end-of-block symbol, and the final block must be padded out to a byte boundary. There is NO 2-byte zlib header (0x78 ...) and NO trailing 4-byte Adler-32 - both are common generator mistakes and both make inflate fail at once. A stored block inside the stream needs LEN/NLEN as a 16-bit pair with NLEN == ~LEN. Must inflate to exactly frUncompressedSize bytes.
8.generation: call any deflate library in raw mode (zlib deflateInit2 with windowBits -15, Python zlib.compressobj(..., wbits=-15), miniz tdefl with the zlib-header flag clear).

9.requirement: As method 8 but with a 64 KiB window and distance codes up to 32, so it inflates only under a Deflate64-capable decoder.

10.requirement: LZ77 sliding window plus two or three Shannon-Fano trees, parameterised by frFlags bits 1-2 (0x0002 = 3 trees / 8 KiB window, 0x0004 = 2 trees / 4 KiB window).
10.generation: emit only with a dedicated imploder.

12.requirement: A complete bzip2 stream: 'BZh' magic, a block-size digit '1'-'9', at least one 0x314159265359 block, then the 0x177245385090 stream footer carrying the combined CRC, bit-aligned to a byte.
12.generation: call bzip2 and take the whole output.

14.requirement: ZIP's own LZMA framing, not a bare .lzma file: a 2-byte LZMA SDK version (major, minor), a 2-byte little-endian size of the properties field (normally 5), the 5-byte properties (packed lc/lp/pb byte plus 4-byte dictionary size), then the raw LZMA stream terminated by an end-of-stream marker.
14.generation: call an LZMA encoder and prepend the 9-byte ZIP header.

18.generation: practically unavailable; the value stays legal and simply produces a shallow parse.

96.requirement: A complete JPEG per the WinZip JPEG method note: SOI 0xFFD8 first, a valid marker sequence with an SOS segment, EOI 0xFFD9 last.
96.generation: emit any real JPEG file's bytes.

97.requirement: A WavPack stream beginning with the 'wvpk' block header and a correct ckSize for every block.

98.requirement: A PPMd stream preceded by ZIP's PPMd parameters (version byte plus the order/memory settings the encoder used); the decoder re-initialises the model from those parameters, so header and stream must agree.
98.generation: emit only with a PPMd encoder that exposes its model parameters.

99.codec: none - COMP_WzAES is a redirection, not a codec
99.requirement: The real codec is EXTRAFIELD.deCompression and the payload layout is SaltValue (8/12/16 bytes chosen by EXTRAFIELD.Strength) + PassVerification (2 bytes) + that codec's stream + AuthenticationCode (10 bytes); frUncompressedSize counts the plaintext while frCompressedSize counts the whole envelope.
99.generation: emit method 0 or 8 inside the envelope; without the passphrase the AES layer cannot be produced, so this value is a structure exercise rather than a decryptable one.

1.requirement: LZ77 with a 4096-entry byte-oriented dictionary and no entropy coding: each token is a literal byte or a length/distance pair introduced by a leading marker byte.

2.requirement: Byte-oriented LZ77 whose minimum match length is set by the level; level 1 is the least aggressive of the four.

5.requirement: As method 2 at level 4, the most aggressive of the reduced family.

6.requirement: The original PKWARE implode: a 4 KiB or 8 KiB sliding window selected by frFlags bit 2, with 64-entry Shannon-Fano trees for literals and lengths.

7.requirement: Reserved by the specification for a tokenizing compressor that was never published, so any bytes are as good as any others; the value must still be offered because the enum defines it.
7.generation: not producible; keep the value legal and let the decoder take its unsupported-method branch.

ZIPFILERECORD.frData.notes: The field is declared four times in four mutually exclusive branches - line 433 (strong encryption: frCompressedSize minus IVSize, Size and 6), line 455 (WinZip AE: frCompressedSize minus 12 minus the salt), line 460 (ordinary: exactly frCompressedSize) and line 471 (streamed: posNext - posCurrent, the distance to the next data-descriptor signature) - and all four measure the same bytes in the file differently. The rule that outranks the rest: derive the payload from frUncompressedSize and the plaintext, never pick a plaintext that happens to fit a precomputed payload. Methods 0 and 8 are the two a generator can always emit correctly and are the preferred values; the exotic methods stay in codec_by_value because each is a separate branch in a decoder that supports it.

ZIPFILERECORD.SaltValue.tier_rationale: Its length is not free: the template derives it from a switch on EXTRAFIELD.Strength (lines 440-451) and then subtracts it from frCompressedSize at line 455, so a salt of the wrong width misplaces the whole WinZip-AE envelope and the record desynchronises - a structural refusal, not a cosmetic difference.
ZIPFILERECORD.SaltValue.description: The AES salt that opens a WinZip AE-encrypted entry's payload, immediately before the 2-byte password verification value.

evidence.note: WinZip AE-1/AE-2: the encrypted file data begins with a salt of 8, 12 or 16 bytes for AES-128, AES-192 and AES-256 respectively, followed by a 2-byte password verification value, the encrypted data and a 10-byte authentication code.

ZIPFILERECORD.SaltValue.algorithm: byte count selected by EXTRAFIELD.Strength: 8 for AES128 (1), 12 for AES192 (2), 16 for AES256 (3)
ZIPFILERECORD.SaltValue.notes: The salt bytes themselves are random and free - nothing inspects them - but the COUNT is fixed by the AES strength and feeds the payload arithmetic. The template only knows the count when the preceding extra field really is EH_WzAES (the test at line 438); if that test fails, lenSalt stays 0 and the whole envelope shifts, which is itself a divergence worth generating.

ZIPFILERECORD.PassVerification.tier_rationale: It is 2 bytes of key-derived crypto material: no structure parser reads them, and only a decrypter that already holds the passphrase can tell right from wrong - at which point the entry was never going to yield useful work without the key. Only its position (right after the salt) and its fixed 2-byte width matter, and those are carried by frCompressedSize.
ZIPFILERECORD.PassVerification.description: The WinZip AE password verification value, stored immediately after the salt and immediately before the encrypted data.

evidence.note: WinZip AE: a 2-byte value derived from the password with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1, used to reject a wrong password before decrypting anything.

ZIPFILERECORD.PassVerification.notes: Asked-and-answered opaque field: the specification does define how it is computed, but it cannot be produced without the passphrase, so leave it free. Its fixed 2-byte width is already accounted for in the '- 12' at line 455 (2 bytes PassVerification + 10 bytes AuthenticationCode).

ZIPFILERECORD.AuthenticationCode.tier_rationale: It is a message authentication code, i.e. a checksum, and the tier definitions put checksums in Tier A; more practically its width is a hard structural fact - exactly 10 bytes, inside frCompressedSize - and getting the width wrong shifts every byte that follows, which makes the record desynchronise.
ZIPFILERECORD.AuthenticationCode.description: The WinZip AE authentication code trailing the encrypted data of the entry.
