evidence.note: WinZip AE: the last 10 bytes of the encrypted file data are the first 80 bits of the HMAC-SHA1 computed over the ciphertext with the key derived from the password and the salt.

ZIPFILERECORD.AuthenticationCode.algorithm: fixed byte count of 10 (the 80-bit truncation of HMAC-SHA1 over the ciphertext)
ZIPFILERECORD.AuthenticationCode.notes: The width is exactly 10 and is the '+ 10' half of the '- 12' at line 455, so treat that part as Tier A even though the bytes cannot be. The HMAC itself needs the passphrase: a generator without it must emit 10 arbitrary bytes and accept that a decrypting decoder will report an authentication failure - the structure parse up to that point is still fully exercised.

ZIPFILERECORD.dataDescr.tier_rationale: Whether an entry carries a data descriptor at all is a pure presence/absence choice made by ZIPFILERECORD.frFlags bit 3, so there is no decoder value check to fail on the instance itself - and the four fields inside it are all Tier A. Pinning the choice to either branch would delete a whole code path from the corpus: with it fixed absent the streaming branch of the template (the frCompressedSize == 0 test at line 462 and the FindFirst scan at line 468) would never run, and with it fixed present every entry would have to be streamed. Both branches are legitimate file shapes, so the presence is sampled.
ZIPFILERECORD.dataDescr.description: The optional ZIPDATADESCR record appended after the compressed payload of a streamed entry, instantiated inside ZIPFILERECORD.

evidence.note: APPNOTE 4.3.9 data descriptor: when bit 3 of the general purpose bit flag is set the crc-32 and the compressed and uncompressed sizes were not known when the local header was written, so they are appended after the compressed data; the four-byte signature 0x08074b50 is optional in the specification but the CRC and both sizes are mandatory and must agree with the central directory copies.

ZIPFILERECORD.dataDescr.notes: Emit it if and only if ZIPFILERECORD.frFlags bit 3 (FLAG_DescriptorUsedMask, 0x0008) is set; the two dependencies that make it required and forbidden in the opposite branch state this formally. The template reaches the instance only in the streaming branch - frCompressedSize == 0 together with bit 3 at line 462 - and locates the record by scanning forward for 0x08074B50 with FindFirst (line 468), then sizes frData as posNext - posCurrent (line 471), so a streamed entry must write 0 in frCrc, frCompressedSize and frUncompressedSize and carry the real values here and in the central directory copy. Nothing about the instance itself is a value a generator picks, which is why it stays Tier C while its four members are Tier A.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deSignature.tier_rationale: The dispatcher reads the dword at the current offset (line 618) and compares it against S_ZIPDIRENTRY (line 639); any other value falls to the else at line 664, warns 'Unknown ZIP tag encountered. Template stopped.' and returns -1, so the whole central directory is never read. Real decoders are stricter still: the central directory signature is how they locate and count every entry.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deSignature.description: The 4-byte signature that begins a central directory entry (0x02014b50).

evidence.note: APPNOTE central directory file header: signature = 0x02014b50; the .bt declares the literal in the SignatureTYPE enum at line 37.

lookahead.note: Same call site as ZIPFILERECORD.frSignature; the full seven-value set is mined there and 0x02014b50 selects the ZIPDIRENTRY branch at lines 639-643.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deSignature.notes: Emit 0x02014B50 at the start of every central-directory record (matched at line 639, abort at line 664). Every copy must fall inside the extent ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDirectoryOffset and ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDirectorySize describe, and their number must equal ZIPENDLOCATOR.elEntriesInDirectory.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deVersionMadeBy.tier_rationale: Covered by the shared VERECORD entries: a wrong version-made-by word produces at most a warning and the archive still opens, so it fails the Tier A test, but both of its bytes have finite legal sets (the APPNOTE version table and the host-system enumeration), which is Tier B.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deVersionMadeBy.description: The version and host system that wrote this entry: low byte is the version, high byte is the operating system whose external-attribute semantics apply.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deVersionMadeBy.notes: The version byte uses the same legal set as VERECORD.Version; the host byte uses the same 20-value set as VERECORD.HostOS (OS_FAT 0 through OS_OSX 19). The host byte is what makes ZIPDIRENTRY.deExternalAttributes mean DOS attributes or Unix mode bits, so varying it is a genuine diversity axis that reaches different permission-handling code in every decoder.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deVersionToExtract.tier_rationale: Same reasoning as the version fields elsewhere: Info-ZIP warns 'ZIP file version N.N unsupported' (PK_WARN) and keeps extracting rather than refusing the file, so it is not Tier A; the legal set is the finite APPNOTE version table, which is Tier B.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deVersionToExtract.description: The minimum ZIP version a reader needs in order to extract this entry.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deVersionToExtract.notes: Must be at least the level the entry's own features imply: 20 for stored/deflate, 21 for Deflate64, 45 the moment a ZIP64 extra field carries a size or offset, 46 for bzip2, 50/51/63 for DES/AES/LZMA-PPMd-WinZip-AE, 62 when the central directory itself is encrypted. The host byte of this word is conventionally 0 or 3 rather than meaningful; nothing validates it.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deFlags.tier_rationale: Same field type and same reasoning as ZIPFILERECORD.frFlags: a wrong flag word changes which decryption, streaming and naming path an entry takes but never makes a conforming decoder refuse the archive, and the legal set is the finite FLAGTYPE bitmask - Tier B.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deFlags.description: The general purpose bit flag as recorded in the central directory for this entry; it is a copy of the local header's ZIPFILERECORD.frFlags.

evidence.note: APPNOTE central directory file header: general purpose bit flag, the same 16-bit mask as the local header's; when the central directory itself is encrypted (bit 13) selected local-header values are masked.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deFlags.completeness_reason: As for ZIPFILERECORD.frFlags: the legal set is every OR-combination of valid_bits, all 65536 values 0-65535, and nothing outside the listed values is excluded. Bit 13 (FLAG_CDEncrypted) is the one bit whose meaning differs here rather than in the local header.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deFlags.notes: Should equal ZIPFILERECORD.frFlags for the same entry: decoders read this copy, not the local one, when they decide whether to look for a data descriptor or a UTF-8 name. All 16 FLAGTYPE members are recorded and none dropped.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deCompression.tier_rationale: Same field type and same reasoning as ZIPFILERECORD.frCompression: an unsupported method makes a decoder refuse that one entry rather than the archive, and the legal set is the finite COMPTYPE enumeration where every member selects a different decompression branch - Tier B.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deCompression.description: The compression method recorded in the central directory for this entry; it is the copy a decoder actually acts on.

evidence.note: APPNOTE central directory file header: compression method, the same table as the local header's.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deCompression.notes: All 19 COMPTYPE members listed, none dropped, same set as ZIPFILERECORD.frCompression. Must agree with the local header's value for the same entry - a mismatch makes Info-ZIP complain about a corrupt directory - and it, not frCompression, is what a decoder consults to choose the codec for ZIPFILERECORD.frData's bytes.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileTime.tier_rationale: Timestamps are named Tier C outright: the central directory's MS-DOS time word is stored and displayed, never validated, so any value still yields an archive every decoder opens and constraining it would cost diversity for no depth.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileTime.description: The entry's last-modification time as an MS-DOS time word, central directory copy.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileTime.notes: Left free. Conventionally equals ZIPFILERECORD.frFileTime, but a mismatch is not an error to any decoder; an EH_NTFS extra field can carry a more precise time and takes precedence in decoders that read it.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileDate.tier_rationale: Timestamps are named Tier C outright: the central directory's MS-DOS date word is stored and displayed, never validated, so any value still yields an archive every decoder opens and constraining it would cost diversity for no depth.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileDate.description: The entry's last-modification date as an MS-DOS date word, central directory copy.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileDate.notes: Left free, including month/day combinations no calendar produces, because Info-ZIP clamps rather than rejects. A date word of 0 (1980-00-00) is a common real-world value from tools that had no timestamp to store.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deCrc.tier_rationale: This is the copy of the CRC-32 that decoders actually compare against the value they compute while inflating; a mismatch makes Info-ZIP report 'incorrect data CRC-32' and libzip return ZIP_ER_CRC, so the entry is rejected rather than delivered.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deCrc.description: The CRC-32 of the entry's uncompressed file data, as recorded in the central directory.

evidence.note: APPNOTE central directory file header: crc-32 of the uncompressed file data; for a streamed entry (flags bit 3) the real value lives in the ZIPDATADESCR and this field is updated to it once the payload is complete.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deCrc.covers: the uncompressed expansion of ZIPFILERECORD.frData for this entry
ZIPDIRENTRY.deCrc.notes: Keep it equal to ZIPFILERECORD.frCrc, and to ZIPDATADESCR.ddCRC when the entry is streamed. Exception: a WinZip AE-2 entry (EXTRAFIELD.version == 2) requires 0 here even though AE-1 requires the real CRC.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deCompressedSize.tier_rationale: It bounds how many bytes a decoder feeds to the inflate or copy routine for this entry and is cross-checked against the local header; a wrong count makes extraction fail with 'invalid compressed data' or a length mismatch, so the decoder stops before doing useful work.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deCompressedSize.description: The size in bytes of the entry's compressed payload, central directory copy.

evidence.note: APPNOTE central directory file header: compressed size; write 0xFFFFFFFF here and put the real 64-bit value in the ZIP64 extra field when it does not fit.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deCompressedSize.covers: the same bytes as ZIPFILERECORD.frCompressedSize: the payload plus any WinZip-AE salt, verification value and authentication code, or the strong-encryption header
ZIPDIRENTRY.deCompressedSize.notes: Derive it from the bytes actually emitted. It must equal ZIPFILERECORD.frCompressedSize, or ZIPDATADESCR.ddCompressedSize for a streamed entry. Write 0xFFFFFFFF when the true size needs more than 32 bits and let EXTRAFIELD.efCompressedSize carry it.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deUncompressedSize.tier_rationale: It is the output length a decoder checks its expansion against and the size it pre-allocates; a wrong value makes the extracted entry fail the length check before it is handed to the caller, so the decoder refuses the data.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deUncompressedSize.description: The size in bytes of the entry's file data after decompression, central directory copy.

evidence.note: APPNOTE central directory file header: uncompressed size; write 0xFFFFFFFF here and put the real 64-bit value in the ZIP64 extra field when it does not fit.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deUncompressedSize.covers: the decompressed expansion of ZIPFILERECORD.frData for this entry
ZIPDIRENTRY.deUncompressedSize.notes: Derive it from the plaintext, never shrink the plaintext to fit it. Must equal ZIPFILERECORD.frUncompressedSize, or ZIPDATADESCR.ddUncompressedSize for a streamed entry. For a COMP_WzAES entry it counts the plaintext only, not the AES envelope. Write 0xFFFFFFFF when the true size needs more than 32 bits and let EXTRAFIELD.efOriginalSize carry it.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileNameLength.tier_rationale: It fixes the byte count of ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileName and therefore the position of the extra field that follows in a packed record sequence; getting it wrong makes the central directory unreadable end to end and every entry after the first one is lost, so the decoder stops before doing useful work.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileNameLength.description: The length in bytes of the central directory file name.

evidence.note: APPNOTE central directory file header: file name length (n); deFileName is then read as byte deFileName[deFileNameLength]. ReadUInt(deFileNameLength) at line 500 consumes the field.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileNameLength.notes: Set it from the name bytes actually emitted and never the reverse. Should equal ZIPFILERECORD.frFileNameLength for the same entry, because the name is the archive's only key: a mismatch splits one file into two in every decoder's listing. The field is read with ReadUInt() in the template's own read function, so it must be self-consistent for the entry to render.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deExtraFieldLength.tier_rationale: It bounds the ZIPDIRENTRY.deExtraField loop and fixes where the file comment starts; an over-long value makes the record swallow the following bytes and the directory walk fall out of alignment, so the decoder stops before doing useful work.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deExtraFieldLength.description: The length in bytes of the central directory extra field block.

evidence.note: APPNOTE central directory file header: extra field length (m); ReadUInt(deExtraFieldLength) at line 504 drives the while-loop over the packed EXTRA64FIELD records.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deExtraFieldLength.covers: the whole ZIPDIRENTRY.deExtraField block, including every EXTRA64FIELD.efHeaderID and efDataSize plus the data each efDataSize counts
ZIPDIRENTRY.deExtraFieldLength.notes: Sum the emitted (4 + efDataSize) of every EXTRA64FIELD. It may differ from ZIPFILERECORD.frExtraFieldLength - the central directory's copy legitimately carries an EH_ZIP64 record the local header does not - but each block must match its own length field exactly.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileCommentLength.tier_rationale: It bounds ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileComment and fixes the record's total size, which is what the central-directory walk uses to reach the next entry; a wrong value makes every following entry unreadable, so the decoder stops before doing useful work.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileCommentLength.description: The length in bytes of the per-entry file comment.

evidence.note: APPNOTE central directory file header: file comment length (k); ReadUInt(deFileCommentLength) at line 508 consumes the field.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileCommentLength.notes: There is no local-header counterpart, so this comment exists only in the central directory and its length is the only thing that bounds it. Set it from the bytes emitted.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deDiskNumberStart.tier_rationale: No conforming decoder refuses an archive because this entry claims to start on disk 7 - it only matters when the archive is genuinely split across volumes - but the legal set is a finite enumeration of sentinels and normal values and a wrong one makes a decoder go looking for a volume that does not exist, so Tier B.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deDiskNumberStart.description: The number of the disk on which this entry's local header begins.

evidence.note: APPNOTE central directory file header: disk number start; 0 in every single-volume archive, 0xFFFF as the ZIP64 sentinel with the real 32-bit number in the EH_ZIP64 record and the ZIP64 end-of-central-directory record.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deDiskNumberStart.completeness_reason: Any 16-bit disk number is a legal value for a genuinely multi-volume archive, so the full set is 0-65534 plus the 0xFFFF sentinel; only the two values a single-volume generator ever emits are pinned here.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deDiskNumberStart.notes: Keep it 0 unless the archive really is split. If it is 0xFFFF, the true value must appear in the ZIP64 extra field's disk-number member, which zip-orig.bt leaves commented out at lines 237 and 300 so this template cannot read it; ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64StartDiskNumber and ZIPENDLOCATOR.elStartDiskNumber must agree with it.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deInternalAttributes.tier_rationale: No conforming decoder refuses an entry over these bits - text/binary is a hint that mainframe ports act on and everyone else ignores - but the field is a finite two-bit mask with named meanings, so Tier B rather than C.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deInternalAttributes.description: Internal file attributes: a hint about whether the entry's data is text, plus a mainframe record-length flag.

evidence.note: APPNOTE central directory file header: internal file attributes; bit 0 set means the file is apparently ASCII or text, bit 1 is reserved and controls record-length interpretation on mainframe ports. The .bt types it as a plain ushort with no enum, so the bit meanings come from the APPNOTE only.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deInternalAttributes.completeness_reason: Only bits 0 and 1 are defined; bits 2-15 are unused and any value in them is ignored, so the defined set is all four combinations of the two bits.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deInternalAttributes.notes: Emit 1 for text entries and 0 for binary ones. Decoders that translate line endings on extraction consult this bit, so varying it reaches different code than varying deExternalAttributes.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deExternalAttributes.tier_rationale: No conforming decoder refuses an entry over its permission or attribute word - Info-ZIP's mapattr() just falls through to a default - but the field is the finite FILEATTRIBUTE bitmask and every bit changes what the extracted file becomes on disk (regular, directory, symlink, setuid, read-only), so it is Tier B.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deExternalAttributes.description: External file attributes: the DOS attribute byte in the low word and/or the full Unix st_mode in the high word, selected by VERECORD.HostOS.

evidence.note: APPNOTE central directory file header: external file attributes, host-system dependent; the .bt's typedef enum <uint> FILEATTRIBUTE at lines 315-357 defines all 44 members.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deExternalAttributes.completeness_reason: All 44 FILEATTRIBUTE members are recorded in template order and none dropped. valid_values repeats some numbers (0x00000001 is both DOSReadOnly and UnixOtherExecute, 0x00004000 is both DOSReserved15 and UnixFileDir) because the same bit legitimately carries two meanings and VERECORD.HostOS decides which; valid_bits therefore lists the 28 distinct settable numeric positions.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deExternalAttributes.notes: Read this field through VERECORD.HostOS. For a DOS-family host (OS_FAT, OS_HPFS, OS_NTFS, OS_VFAT) the low word is the DOS attribute byte: 32 (0x20 DOSArchive) for a normal file, 16 (0x10 DOSDirectory) for a directory, 0 for none. For OS_Unix or OS_OSX the high 16 bits hold the whole st_mode, so a 0644 regular file is 2175008768 (0x81A40000) and a 0755 directory is 1106051072 (0x41ED0000); Info-ZIP extracts exactly that mode. Setuid (UnixFileSetUID), sticky (UnixFileSticky) and the symlink file types are the security-relevant bits - a decoder that trusts them creates privileged or redirected files - so varying them is a real depth axis, and the directory bit must agree with the trailing '/' in ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileName or extraction becomes inconsistent.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deHeaderOffset.tier_rationale: This is the only pointer from the central directory to the entry's data: a decoder seeks to it and expects ZIPFILERECORD.frSignature there. A wrong offset makes the seek land outside the file or on bytes that are not a local header, so the entry cannot be read and the decoder aborts before doing useful work.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deHeaderOffset.description: The byte offset, from the start of the archive, of this entry's local file header.

evidence.note: APPNOTE central directory file header: relative offset of local header; 0xFFFFFFFF as the ZIP64 sentinel with the real 64-bit offset in the EH_ZIP64 extra field. The offset is relative to the start of the archive, which for a self-extracting exe means after the stub, and decoders recover from a leading stub by measuring the difference between this value and the directory's own position.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deHeaderOffset.covers: the start byte of the corresponding ZIPFILERECORD
ZIPDIRENTRY.deHeaderOffset.notes: Write the real offset of the local header as emitted. Use 0xFFFFFFFF only when the offset genuinely exceeds 32 bits, and then the ZIP64 extra field's relative-header-offset member must carry the 64-bit value (zip-orig.bt comments it out at lines 236 and 299, so this template reads those bytes as generic EXTRAFIELD.efData). Offsets are relative to the archive start, not to the central directory, and they must be strictly increasing for entries written in order - decoders use them to detect a prepended stub and to validate the directory.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileName.tier_rationale: Text is named Tier C outright: the central directory's name bytes are stored, listed and matched against nothing, and any byte sequence of the declared length still yields an archive the decoder opens, so constraining it would remove the path-traversal, absolute-path, backslash and non-UTF-8 branches that decoders handle specially.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileName.description: The entry's path name as raw bytes in the central directory, with '/' as the directory separator.

evidence.note: Guarded by 'if( deFileNameLength > 0 )' at line 499, so a zero-length name emits no bytes; ReadUInt(deFileNameLength) at line 500 consumes the length.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileName.notes: Only the byte length is constrained; the content is free. This is the name a decoder reports in listings and the key it uses to match a local header, so it should equal ZIPFILERECORD.frFileName byte for byte. A directory entry ends with '/'. When deFlags bit 11 is set the bytes are UTF-8, otherwise CP437 - both are legal and both should be generated. When an EH_InfoZIPUnicodePath record is present its NameCRC32 must match the CRC-32 of these bytes or the decoder keeps this name and ignores the Unicode one.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deExtraField.tier_rationale: How many extra fields a central directory entry carries is a repetition count: any number from zero upward is legal, unknown IDs are ignored by every conforming decoder, and a wrong count costs nothing because the chain is bounded by deExtraFieldLength - so the count stays Tier C while the total byte budget it fills is Tier A.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deExtraField.description: The chain of optional extra fields between the central directory file name and the file comment.

evidence.note: Driven by 'local int len = deExtraFieldLength;' at line 501 and 'while (len > 0)' at line 502, with 'len -= deExtraField.efDataSize + 4;' at line 505; APPNOTE says the extra field is a sequence of variable-length records, each a 2-byte header ID, a 2-byte data size and that many data bytes.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deExtraField.notes: Leave the record count free (0, 1, or many) - it is a genuine diversity axis and each of the ZIP64, Unicode Path, NTFS and WinZip-AE readers is a distinct code path that only runs when the record is present. The hard rule is the loop's exact termination: len starts at deExtraFieldLength and subtracts efDataSize + 4 per record, so the record sizes must sum exactly to deExtraFieldLength, otherwise len goes negative and the template keeps consuming past the record. This block is where the 0xFFFFFFFF sentinels in deCompressedSize, deUncompressedSize, deHeaderOffset and deDiskNumberStart get their real 64-bit values, in that field order and only for the fields actually sentinelled.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileComment.tier_rationale: Text is named Tier C outright: the per-entry comment is displayed and validated against nothing, so any byte sequence of the declared length still yields an archive every decoder opens, and pinning it would delete a free-text axis for no depth.
ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileComment.description: The optional per-entry file comment, present only in the central directory.

evidence.note: Guarded by 'if( deFileCommentLength > 0 )' at line 507, so a zero-length comment emits no bytes; ReadUInt(deFileCommentLength) at line 508 consumes the length. The declared element type is uchar rather than the char used for deFileName, so bytes 0x80-0xFF are not sign-extended when the template displays them.

ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileComment.notes: Only its byte length is constrained; the content is free, including arbitrary binary bytes and no NUL terminator. deFlags bit 11 says the comment is UTF-8 rather than CP437. Most real archives leave it empty, so a zero length is the common case, but a long comment is a distinct code path in decoders that size their listing buffers from it.

ZIPDIGITALSIG.dsSignature.tier_rationale: The dispatcher reads the dword at the current offset (line 618) and compares it against S_ZIPDIGITALSIG (line 644); any other value falls to the else at line 664, warns 'Unknown ZIP tag encountered. Template stopped.' and returns -1, so no further record is parsed. Real decoders use this signature to recognise the archive's digital signature record.
ZIPDIGITALSIG.dsSignature.description: The 4-byte signature that begins a digital signature record (0x05054b50).

evidence.note: APPNOTE digital signature record: signature = 0x05054b50; the .bt declares the literal in the SignatureTYPE enum at line 38. It appears after the central directory and before the end-of-central-directory record, or immediately after a local header's payload for per-entry signatures.

lookahead.note: Same call site as ZIPFILERECORD.frSignature; the full seven-value set is mined there and 0x05054b50 selects the ZIPDIGITALSIG branch at lines 644-648.

ZIPDIGITALSIG.dsSignature.notes: Emit 0x05054B50 only when the archive really carries a digital-signature record (matched at line 644, abort at line 664); omitting the record entirely is the normal case. The dispatcher accepts it anywhere in the record sequence because it matches purely on the dword (lines 618-662), while APPNOTE places it after the central directory.

ZIPDIGITALSIG.dsDataLength.tier_rationale: It is used directly as the length of the dsData array (line 516, guarded at line 515) and therefore fixes the record's total size; a wrong value ends the record at the wrong offset, the next ReadUInt at line 618 misses every signature and the template aborts with 'Unknown ZIP tag encountered. Template stopped.'
ZIPDIGITALSIG.dsDataLength.description: The number of bytes of signature data that follow this field.

evidence.note: APPNOTE digital signature record: size of the signature data; dsData is then read as uchar dsData[dsDataLength] under 'if( dsDataLength > 0 )' at line 515, so a zero length emits no data bytes.

ZIPDIGITALSIG.dsDataLength.notes: Set it from the signature bytes actually emitted. Real signatures are PKCS#7 blobs whose length varies with the certificate chain, so leaving the value free within 0-65535 is legitimate as long as the data length matches. Zero is legal and produces a header-only record.

ZIPDIGITALSIG.dsData.tier_rationale: Opaque crypto material is Tier C: no mainstream decoder verifies a ZIP digital signature - it is skipped or ignored entirely - so its bytes are never validated against anything and pinning them would buy no depth while deleting free bytes.
ZIPDIGITALSIG.dsData.description: The raw digital signature bytes, a PKCS#7 signed-data blob in the original specification.

evidence.note: Declared uchar rather than char, so bytes 0x80-0xFF are not sign-extended when the template displays them; bounded only by dsDataLength.

ZIPDIGITALSIG.dsData.notes: Only its byte length is constrained. Fill it with arbitrary bytes: Info-ZIP, libzip and 7-Zip all step over this record without parsing it, so its content reaches no validation logic. Emitting a record at all is still worth doing because its presence changes where the end-of-central-directory record is found by a backward signature scan.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64Signature.tier_rationale: The dispatcher reads the dword at the current offset (line 618) and compares it against S_ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD (line 649); any other value falls to the else at line 664, warns 'Unknown ZIP tag encountered. Template stopped.' and returns -1. Real decoders use this signature to find the ZIP64 end record and without it every 64-bit size and offset in the archive is unreachable.
ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64Signature.description: The 4-byte signature that begins the ZIP64 end of central directory record (0x06064b50).

evidence.note: APPNOTE Zip64 end of central directory record: signature = 0x06064b50; the .bt declares the literal in the SignatureTYPE enum at line 39. It sits immediately before the ZIP64 end-of-central-directory locator.

lookahead.note: Same call site as ZIPFILERECORD.frSignature; the full seven-value set is mined there and 0x06064b50 selects the ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD branch at lines 649-653.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64Signature.notes: Emit 0x06064B50 at the start of the ZIP64 end record (matched at line 649). ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elDirectoryOffset must point exactly at this byte, and the record must be followed immediately by the 20-byte locator and then by ZIPENDLOCATOR.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64DirectoryReco.tier_rationale: Every following field in this record is conditionally read against this value (lines 523-541: 'if (elr64DirectoryRecordSize > 1)', '> 2', '> 4', '> 8', '> 12', '> 20', '> 28', '> 36', '> 44'), and the extensible data sector's array length is computed from it directly (line 541). A wrong value therefore truncates or over-reads the record, the dispatcher's next ReadUInt at line 618 misses every signature and the template aborts - the decoder stops before doing useful work.
ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64DirectoryReco.description: The size in bytes of the remainder of the ZIP64 end of central directory record, not counting the signature and this field itself.

evidence.note: APPNOTE Zip64 end of central directory record: 'size of zip64 end of central directory record', defined as the total record size minus 12; the fixed portion is 44 bytes and any extensible data sector adds to it. The .bt reads it as int64 and then uses it as the presence threshold for each subsequent field.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64DirectoryReco.covers: every byte of this record after this field: elr64VersionMadeBy, elr64VersionToExtract, el64DiskNumber, el64StartDiskNumber, el64EntriesOnDisk, el64EntriesInDirectory, el64DirectorySize, el64DirectoryOffset and DataSect
ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64DirectoryReco.notes: Write 44 for a standard record with no extensible data sector, and 44 + (sector length) when one is present. The APPNOTE's own arithmetic is record-size-minus-12, so the total record is this value plus 12 bytes. Because the .bt uses it as a presence test rather than a pure length, a value below 44 makes the template silently skip the trailing fields instead of reporting a short record - a divergence worth generating against, since real decoders reject a ZIP64 end record smaller than 44.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64VersionMadeBy.tier_rationale: Covered by the shared VERECORD entries: a wrong version-made-by word here produces at most a warning and the archive still opens, so it fails the Tier A test, but both of its bytes have finite legal sets (the APPNOTE version table and the host-system enumeration), which is Tier B.
ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64VersionMadeBy.description: The version and host system that wrote the ZIP64 end of central directory record.

evidence.note: Read only when 'if (elr64DirectoryRecordSize > 1)' at line 523 holds, so a record whose size field claims fewer than 2 remaining bytes leaves it absent; APPNOTE Zip64 end of central directory record: version made by.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64VersionMadeBy.notes: The version byte uses the same legal set as VERECORD.Version and the host byte the same 20-value set as VERECORD.HostOS. Because this record exists only to carry ZIP64 values, 45 (4.5) is the value every real writer emits here.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64VersionToExtr.tier_rationale: Same reasoning as the version fields elsewhere: Info-ZIP warns 'ZIP file version N.N unsupported' (PK_WARN) and keeps reading rather than refusing the file, so it is not Tier A; the legal set is the finite APPNOTE version table, which is Tier B.
ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64VersionToExtr.description: The minimum ZIP version a reader needs in order to interpret this ZIP64 end of central directory record.

evidence.note: Read only when 'if (elr64DirectoryRecordSize > 2)' at line 525 holds; APPNOTE Zip64 end of central directory record: version needed to extract.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64VersionToExtr.notes: Must be at least 45 the moment this record exists at all, because ZIP64 format extensions are what introduced it; 62 additionally when the central directory is itself encrypted. The host byte of this word is conventionally 0 or 3 and nothing validates it.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DiskNumber.tier_rationale: No conforming decoder refuses an archive over the disk number recorded here - it only matters for genuinely split archives - but the legal set is a finite enumeration of the normal value and the multi-volume sentinel, so Tier B.
ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DiskNumber.description: The number of this disk, as a full 32-bit value rather than the 16-bit field the end-of-central-directory record can hold.

evidence.note: Read only when 'if (elr64DirectoryRecordSize > 4)' at line 527 holds; APPNOTE Zip64 end of central directory record: number of this disk.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DiskNumber.completeness_reason: Any 32-bit disk number is legal for a genuinely multi-volume archive, so the full set is 0-4294967294 plus the sentinel; only the two values a single-volume generator emits are pinned here.
ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DiskNumber.notes: Keep it 0 unless the archive is really split. ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDiskNumber then reads 0xFFFF as its sentinel and this field carries the true number.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64StartDiskNumbe.tier_rationale: No conforming decoder refuses an archive over this value - it selects which volume the central directory starts on, which is meaningless for a single-file archive - but the legal set is a finite enumeration of the normal value and the multi-volume sentinel, so Tier B.
ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64StartDiskNumbe.description: The number of the disk on which the central directory starts.

evidence.note: Read only when 'if (elr64DirectoryRecordSize > 8)' at line 529 holds; APPNOTE Zip64 end of central directory record: number of the disk with the start of the central directory.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64StartDiskNumbe.completeness_reason: Any 32-bit disk number is legal for a genuinely multi-volume archive, so the full set is 0-4294967294 plus the sentinel; only the two values a single-volume generator emits are pinned here.
ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64StartDiskNumbe.notes: Keep it 0 unless the archive is really split, and keep it equal to ZIPENDLOCATOR.elStartDiskNumber once that field's 0xFFFF sentinel is resolved through this one. el64DirectoryOffset is relative to the start of this disk, not to the start of volume 0.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64EntriesOnDisk.tier_rationale: A decoder reads exactly this many central directory records from this volume; a count larger than the records present makes it run off the end of the directory into bytes that are not ZIPDIRENTRY signatures, so it aborts before doing useful work.
ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64EntriesOnDisk.description: The total number of central directory entries recorded on this disk, as a full 64-bit count.

evidence.note: Read only when 'if (elr64DirectoryRecordSize > 12)' at line 531 holds; APPNOTE Zip64 end of central directory record: total number of entries in the central directory on this disk.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64EntriesOnDisk.covers: every ZIPDIRENTRY record emitted on this disk
ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64EntriesOnDisk.notes: Count the ZIPDIRENTRY records actually written on this volume and write that number. For a single-volume archive it equals el64EntriesInDirectory. ZIPENDLOCATOR.elEntriesOnDisk must read 0xFFFF whenever this value exceeds 65535, and must otherwise agree with it exactly.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64EntriesInDirec.tier_rationale: It is the entry count every decoder cross-checks against the directory it walks; a count larger than the records present makes the walk run past the directory into non-signature bytes and the parse aborts, so the decoder stops before doing useful work.
ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64EntriesInDirec.description: The total number of entries in the whole central directory, as a full 64-bit count.

evidence.note: Read only when 'if (elr64DirectoryRecordSize > 20)' at line 533 holds; APPNOTE Zip64 end of central directory record: total number of entries in the central directory.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64EntriesInDirec.covers: every ZIPDIRENTRY record in the archive, across all volumes
ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64EntriesInDirec.notes: Count the ZIPDIRENTRY records actually written and write that number; it must be at least el64EntriesOnDisk and equal to it for a single-volume archive. ZIPENDLOCATOR.elEntriesInDirectory must read 0xFFFF whenever this exceeds 65535 and must otherwise agree exactly - Info-ZIP compares the two and warns when they differ.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DirectorySize.tier_rationale: It is the byte budget a decoder allows for walking the central directory; a value smaller than the directory actually is makes the walk stop early and report missing entries, and a larger one makes it read past the directory into the end records, so the decoder stops before doing useful work.
ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DirectorySize.description: The size in bytes of the whole central directory, as a full 64-bit count.

evidence.note: Read only when 'if (elr64DirectoryRecordSize > 28)' at line 535 holds; APPNOTE Zip64 end of central directory record: size of the central directory.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DirectorySize.covers: every ZIPDIRENTRY record in the archive, from the first deSignature byte to the last deFileComment byte, across all volumes
ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DirectorySize.notes: Sum the emitted size of every ZIPDIRENTRY (46 bytes of fixed fields plus deFileNameLength + deExtraFieldLength + deFileCommentLength). ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDirectorySize must read 0xFFFFFFFF whenever this exceeds 32 bits and must otherwise agree exactly. el64DirectoryOffset + el64DirectorySize must land exactly on the first byte of the ZIP64 end record for a single-volume archive.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DirectoryOffse.tier_rationale: It is the seek target for the whole central directory: a decoder jumps to it and expects ZIPDIRENTRY.deSignature there. A wrong offset lands the seek outside the file or on non-directory bytes, so no entry can be listed and the decoder aborts before doing useful work.
ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DirectoryOffse.description: The offset of the start of the central directory relative to the starting disk number, as a full 64-bit value.

evidence.note: Read only when 'if (elr64DirectoryRecordSize > 36)' at line 537 holds; APPNOTE Zip64 end of central directory record: offset of start of central directory with respect to the starting disk number.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DirectoryOffse.covers: the start byte of the first ZIPDIRENTRY record
ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DirectoryOffse.notes: Write the real byte offset of the first ZIPDIRENTRY as emitted, relative to the start of el64StartDiskNumber (which for a single-volume archive is the start of the file, after any self-extracting stub). ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDirectoryOffset must read 0xFFFFFFFF whenever this exceeds 32 bits and must otherwise agree exactly. Do not confuse this with ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elDirectoryOffset, which points at this record instead of at the directory.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.DataSect.tier_rationale: The extensible data sector is reserved for future PKWARE use and every mainstream decoder steps over it unread; its bytes are validated against nothing, so pinning them would buy no depth while removing a free-byte axis.
ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.DataSect.description: The optional extensible data sector that follows the fixed 44 bytes of the ZIP64 end of central directory record.

evidence.note: Read only inside 'if (elr64DirectoryRecordSize > 44)' at line 539; the commented-out loop at lines 542-547 shows the author's intent to parse it as a chain of EXTRA64FIELD records, which the shipped template does not do.

ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.DataSect.notes: Omit it entirely and set elr64DirectoryRecordSize to 44 for the normal case. When present its length is exactly elr64DirectoryRecordSize - 44 and its content is free. The APPNOTE describes it as a sequence of (header ID, data size, data) records like an extra field, so a generator that wants to exercise that path should emit well-formed records - but nothing in a shipping decoder parses them.

ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elSignature.tier_rationale: The dispatcher reads the dword at the current offset (line 618) and compares it against S_ZIP64ENDLOCATOR (line 654); any other value falls to the else at line 664, warns 'Unknown ZIP tag encountered. Template stopped.' and returns -1. Real decoders find the ZIP64 end record through this locator, so without it the 64-bit sizes and offsets are unreachable and a large archive is reported as corrupt.
ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elSignature.description: The 4-byte signature that begins the ZIP64 end of central directory locator (0x07064b50).

evidence.note: APPNOTE Zip64 end of central directory locator: signature = 0x07064b50; the .bt declares the literal in the SignatureTYPE enum at line 40. It sits between the ZIP64 end record and the ordinary end-of-central-directory record, exactly 20 bytes before the latter.

lookahead.note: Same call site as ZIPFILERECORD.frSignature; the full seven-value set is mined there and 0x07064b50 selects the ZIP64ENDLOCATOR branch at lines 654-658.

ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elSignature.notes: Emit 0x07064B50 at the start of the ZIP64 end-of-central-directory locator (matched at line 654). This marker's presence or absence selects the ZIP64 tail, so emit it only together with ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD - immediately after that record and immediately before ZIPENDLOCATOR.

ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elStartDiskNumber.tier_rationale: No conforming decoder refuses an archive over this value - it only matters for genuinely split archives - but the legal set is a finite enumeration whose single normal member is 0, so Tier B rather than A.
ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elStartDiskNumber.description: The number of the disk on which the ZIP64 end of central directory record starts.

evidence.note: APPNOTE Zip64 end of central directory locator: number of the disk with the start of the zip64 end of central directory record.

ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elStartDiskNumber.completeness_reason: Any 32-bit disk number is legal for a genuinely multi-volume archive; only 0 is pinned because it is the sole value a single-volume generator emits.
ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elStartDiskNumber.notes: Keep it 0 for a single-volume archive. elDirectoryOffset is relative to the start of this disk, so a non-zero value here changes what that offset means.

ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elDirectoryOffset.tier_rationale: It is the only pointer from the fixed-size tail of the archive to the ZIP64 end record: a decoder seeks to it and expects ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64Signature there. A wrong offset makes the seek land on non-signature bytes, every 64-bit size and offset becomes unreachable and the archive is reported corrupt - the decoder stops before doing useful work.
ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elDirectoryOffset.description: The relative offset of the ZIP64 end of central directory record, measured from the start of the disk named by ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elStartDiskNumber.

evidence.note: APPNOTE Zip64 end of central directory locator: relative offset of the zip64 end of central directory record. The .bt's field name says 'directory' but the value points at the ZIP64 end record, not at the central directory.

ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elDirectoryOffset.covers: the start byte of the ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD
ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elDirectoryOffset.notes: Write the real byte offset of the ZIP64 end record as emitted. For a single-volume archive it is ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DirectoryOffset + el64DirectorySize, i.e. immediately after the central directory, and this locator itself then begins 20 bytes later. Despite the name it does not point at the central directory - that is ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DirectoryOffset.

ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elEntriesInDirectory.tier_rationale: The .bt names this field as an entry count but the APPNOTE defines the locator's fourth field as the total number of disks; either way no conforming decoder refuses an archive over it, and its legal set is a finite enumeration whose single normal member is 1, so Tier B.
ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elEntriesInDirectory.description: The total number of disks in the archive, per the APPNOTE's ZIP64 end-of-central-directory locator layout; the .bt calls it elEntriesInDirectory.

evidence.note: APPNOTE Zip64 end of central directory locator: total number of disks. The .bt's name is a misnomer carried over from ZIPENDLOCATOR.elEntriesInDirectory; nothing in the template reads the value back.

ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elEntriesInDirectory.completeness_reason: Any 32-bit disk count is legal for a genuinely multi-volume archive; only 1 is pinned because it is the sole value a single-volume generator emits.
ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elEntriesInDirectory.notes: Write 1 for a single-volume archive. Because the field is named as an entry count but defined as a disk count, this is a genuine template/specification divergence: a generator that follows the .bt's name writes the entry count here and every conforming decoder still opens the archive, since nothing validates it. Generating both readings is worthwhile precisely because it exposes which decoders consult the field at all.

ZIPENDLOCATOR.elSignature.tier_rationale: The dispatcher reads the dword at the current offset (line 618) and compares it against S_ZIPENDLOCATOR (line 659); any other value falls to the else at line 664, warns 'Unknown ZIP tag encountered. Template stopped.' and returns -1. Real decoders are stricter still: they locate the whole archive by scanning backwards from end-of-file for exactly these four bytes, so a wrong signature means the file is not recognised as a ZIP at all.
ZIPENDLOCATOR.elSignature.description: The 4-byte signature that begins the end of central directory record (0x06054b50).

evidence.note: APPNOTE end of central directory record: signature = 0x06054b50; the .bt declares the literal in the SignatureTYPE enum at line 41. This is the last record in the archive and the anchor every decoder starts from.

lookahead.note: Same call site as ZIPFILERECORD.frSignature; the full seven-value set is mined there and 0x06054b50 selects the ZIPENDLOCATOR branch at lines 659-663. A backward-scanning decoder looks for this dword in the last 65557 bytes of the file (22 fixed bytes plus a 65535-byte comment).

ZIPENDLOCATOR.elSignature.notes: Emit 0x06054B50 exactly once, in the last record of the archive (matched at line 659): ZIPENDLOCATOR.elComment follows it and nothing may follow that comment. Decoders find the directory by scanning backwards from the end of the file for this dword.

ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDiskNumber.tier_rationale: No conforming decoder refuses an archive over this value - it only matters for genuinely split archives - but the legal set is a finite enumeration of the normal value and the ZIP64 sentinel, so Tier B.

evidence.note: APPNOTE end of central directory record: number of this disk; 0xFFFF is the ZIP64 sentinel and the real value then lives in ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DiskNumber.

ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDiskNumber.completeness_reason: Any 16-bit disk number is legal for a genuinely multi-volume archive, so the full set is 0-65534 plus the 0xFFFF sentinel; only the two values a single-volume generator ever emits are pinned here.
ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDiskNumber.notes: Keep it 0 unless the archive is really split or genuinely exceeds 16 bits, in which case write 0xFFFF and let ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DiskNumber carry the true number. Writing 0xFFFF without a ZIP64 end record present makes every decoder report a corrupt multi-volume archive.

ZIPENDLOCATOR.elStartDiskNumber.tier_rationale: No conforming decoder refuses an archive over this value - it selects which volume the central directory starts on, which is meaningless for a single-file archive - but the legal set is a finite enumeration of the normal value and the ZIP64 sentinel, so Tier B.
ZIPENDLOCATOR.elStartDiskNumber.description: The number of the disk on which the central directory starts.

evidence.note: APPNOTE end of central directory record: number of the disk with the start of the central directory; 0xFFFF is the ZIP64 sentinel and the real value then lives in ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64StartDiskNumber.

ZIPENDLOCATOR.elStartDiskNumber.completeness_reason: Any 16-bit disk number is legal for a genuinely multi-volume archive, so the full set is 0-65534 plus the 0xFFFF sentinel; only the two values a single-volume generator ever emits are pinned here.
ZIPENDLOCATOR.elStartDiskNumber.notes: Keep it 0 unless the archive is really split or genuinely exceeds 16 bits, in which case write 0xFFFF and let ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64StartDiskNumber carry the true number. elDirectoryOffset is relative to the start of this disk.

ZIPENDLOCATOR.elEntriesOnDisk.tier_rationale: A decoder reads exactly this many central directory records from this volume; a count larger than the records present makes the walk run off the end of the directory into bytes that are not ZIPDIRENTRY signatures, so it aborts before doing useful work.
ZIPENDLOCATOR.elEntriesOnDisk.description: The number of central directory entries recorded on this disk.

evidence.note: APPNOTE end of central directory record: total number of entries in the central directory on this disk; 0xFFFF is the ZIP64 sentinel and the real value then lives in ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64EntriesOnDisk.

ZIPENDLOCATOR.elEntriesOnDisk.covers: every ZIPDIRENTRY record emitted on this disk
ZIPENDLOCATOR.elEntriesOnDisk.notes: Count the ZIPDIRENTRY records actually written on this volume and write that number. For a single-volume archive it equals elEntriesInDirectory. Write 0xFFFF as the sentinel when the true count exceeds 65534, and then a ZIP64 end record must be present carrying it.

ZIPENDLOCATOR.elEntriesInDirectory.tier_rationale: It is the entry count every decoder cross-checks against the directory it walks; a count larger than the records present makes the walk run past the directory into non-signature bytes and the parse aborts, so the decoder stops before doing useful work.
ZIPENDLOCATOR.elEntriesInDirectory.description: The total number of entries in the whole central directory.

evidence.note: APPNOTE end of central directory record: total number of entries in the central directory; 0xFFFF is the ZIP64 sentinel and the real value then lives in ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64EntriesInDirectory.

ZIPENDLOCATOR.elEntriesInDirectory.covers: every ZIPDIRENTRY record in the archive, across all volumes
ZIPENDLOCATOR.elEntriesInDirectory.notes: Count the ZIPDIRENTRY records actually written and write that number; it must be at least elEntriesOnDisk and equal to it for a single-volume archive. Write 0xFFFF as the sentinel when the true count exceeds 65534, and then a ZIP64 end record must be present carrying it. Info-ZIP compares this against the number of records it actually walks and warns 'extra entry' or 'missing entry' when they disagree.

ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDirectorySize.tier_rationale: It is the byte budget a decoder allows for walking the central directory; a value smaller than the directory actually is makes the walk stop early and report missing entries, and a larger one makes it read past the directory into the end records, so the decoder stops before doing useful work.
ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDirectorySize.description: The size in bytes of the whole central directory.

evidence.note: APPNOTE end of central directory record: size of the central directory; 0xFFFFFFFF is the ZIP64 sentinel and the real value then lives in ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DirectorySize.

ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDirectorySize.covers: every ZIPDIRENTRY record in the archive, from the first deSignature byte to the last deFileComment byte, across all volumes
ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDirectorySize.notes: Sum the emitted size of every ZIPDIRENTRY (46 bytes of fixed fields plus deFileNameLength + deExtraFieldLength + deFileCommentLength). Write 0xFFFFFFFF as the sentinel when the true size exceeds 32 bits, and then a ZIP64 end record must carry it. elDirectoryOffset + elDirectorySize must land exactly on the first byte after the directory for a single-volume archive.

ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDirectoryOffset.tier_rationale: It is the seek target for the whole central directory: a decoder jumps to it and expects ZIPDIRENTRY.deSignature there. A wrong offset lands the seek outside the file or on non-directory bytes, so no entry can be listed and the decoder aborts before doing useful work.
ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDirectoryOffset.description: The offset of the start of the central directory relative to the starting disk number.

evidence.note: APPNOTE end of central directory record: offset of start of central directory with respect to the starting disk number; 0xFFFFFFFF is the ZIP64 sentinel and the real value then lives in ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DirectoryOffset.

ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDirectoryOffset.covers: the start byte of the first ZIPDIRENTRY record
ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDirectoryOffset.notes: Write the real byte offset of the first ZIPDIRENTRY as emitted, relative to the start of elStartDiskNumber (for a single-volume archive, the start of the file after any self-extracting stub). Write 0xFFFFFFFF as the sentinel when the true offset exceeds 32 bits, and then a ZIP64 end record must carry it. Decoders also use the difference between this value and the offset where they actually found the directory to detect and compensate for a prepended stub, so an intentionally small value here is a legitimate and interesting generation target.

ZIPENDLOCATOR.elCommentLength.tier_rationale: It is the length of the last variable part of the archive and therefore fixes the file's total size; a value that does not match the bytes emitted leaves trailing garbage or a short file, and because decoders find this record by scanning backwards for elSignature and then validate (record offset + 22 + elCommentLength == file size), a wrong value makes the scan reject the record and the archive is reported as not a ZIP - the decoder stops before doing useful work.
ZIPENDLOCATOR.elCommentLength.description: The length in bytes of the archive comment that follows this record.

evidence.note: APPNOTE end of central directory record: .ZIP file comment length (n); elComment is then read as char elComment[elCommentLength] under 'if( elCommentLength > 0 )' at line 570, so a zero length emits no comment bytes.

ZIPENDLOCATOR.elCommentLength.notes: Set it from the comment bytes actually emitted. Because it is the last field of the last record, this value plus the 22 bytes before it must account for every byte to the end of the file; decoders use exactly that arithmetic to decide whether a backward scan found the real end-of-central-directory record or a coincidental signature inside an entry's data or comment. Zero is by far the most common value.

ZIPENDLOCATOR.elComment.tier_rationale: Text is named Tier C outright: the archive comment is displayed and validated against nothing, so any byte sequence of the declared length still yields an archive every decoder opens, and pinning it would delete a free-text axis for no depth.
ZIPENDLOCATOR.elComment.description: The optional whole-archive comment, the last bytes of the file.

evidence.note: Guarded by 'if( elCommentLength > 0 )' at line 570; APPNOTE end of central directory record: .ZIP file comment, up to 65535 bytes.

ZIPENDLOCATOR.elComment.notes: Only its byte length is constrained; the content is free, including arbitrary binary bytes and no NUL terminator. Worth generating with a deliberate copy of the elSignature dword inside it: a naive decoder that scans backwards for 0x06054b50 without checking the length arithmetic will lock onto the embedded copy instead of the real record, which is a real and commonly-hit parsing divergence.

dependencies.description: frFlags bit 3 (0x0008, FLAG_DescriptorUsedMask) declares that the CRC and both sizes were unknown when the local header was written, so a ZIPDATADESCR must follow that entry's data and carry them.
dependencies.notes: The .bt tests this at line 462 together with frCompressedSize == 0, scans forward for S_ZIPDATADESCR with FindFirst (line 468), sizes frData as posNext - posCurrent (line 471) and instantiates ZIPDATADESCR inside the local record at line 474. APPNOTE requires the descriptor's ddCRC, ddCompressedSize and ddUncompressedSize to equal the values the central directory carries for the same entry, so the bit-3 path still has to be self-consistent.

dependencies.description: With frFlags bit 3 clear the local header must already carry the real frCrc, frCompressedSize and frUncompressedSize, and no data descriptor may follow the entry's data.
dependencies.notes: None of the four frData branches at lines 415-476 fires for a descriptor record when bit 3 is clear, so an emitted descriptor is parsed as a stray record by the top-level loop and every decoder treats the mismatch between local and central values as a corruption warning. The three local fields become Tier A calculated values on this path rather than zeros.

dependencies.description: frFlags bit 0 (FLAG_Encrypted) together with bit 6 (FLAG_StrongEncrypted) selects the PKWARE strong-encryption certificate envelope, which must sit between the local header's variable fields and the entry's data.
dependencies.notes: Line 415: 'if ((frFlags & FLAG_Encrypted) && ( frFlags & FLAG_StrongEncrypted))'. The envelope is IVSize/IVData, Size, Format, AlgID, BitLen, Flags, ErdSize/ErdData, Reserved, VSize/VData and VCRC32 (lines 417-432), and frData is then declared as frCompressedSize - IVSize - Size - 6 at line 433, so the envelope's own lengths must be right or the payload boundary is misplaced. Bit 6 alone, without bit 0, selects nothing: the branch requires both.

dependencies.description: frFlags bit 0 with frCompression 99 (COMP_WzAES) selects the WinZip AE envelope: salt, 2-byte password verification value, the encrypted data and a 10-byte authentication code, in that order.
dependencies.notes: Line 435: 'else if ((frFlags & FLAG_Encrypted) && ( frCompression == COMP_WzAES ))', with the salt width switched on EXTRAFIELD.Strength at lines 440-451, SaltValue and PassVerification at lines 453-454, frData as frCompressedSize - 12 - lenSalt at line 455 and the fixed 10-byte AuthenticationCode at line 456. frCompressedSize counts all four parts, which is why the subtraction is 12 (2 + 10) plus the salt.

dependencies.description: AES128 uses an 8-byte salt.
dependencies.notes: Lines 442-444 set lenSalt = 8 for AES128; WinZip AE specifies 8/12/16 for AES-128/192/256. A wrong width misplaces PassVerification, frData and AuthenticationCode for the whole entry.

dependencies.description: AES192 uses a 12-byte salt.
dependencies.notes: Lines 445-447 set lenSalt = 12 for AES192.

dependencies.description: AES256 uses a 16-byte salt.
dependencies.notes: Lines 448-450 set lenSalt = 16 for AES256. Strength values outside 1-3 leave lenSalt at 0 (line 437), which makes frData the full frCompressedSize minus 12 - a silent desynchronisation rather than an error, so a generator must never emit another value here.

then.algorithm: 8 bytes for each ZIP64 value actually present; the template's two fields make 16

dependencies.description: EH_Zip64 (0x0001) selects the ZIP64 extended information block: uncompressed size, compressed size, then relative header offset and disk start number, each 8 bytes, present only for the fields whose 32-bit counterpart holds its sentinel.
dependencies.notes: Lines 233-238 read efOriginalSize and efCompressedSize and leave efHeaderOffset and efDiskNumberStart commented out at lines 236-237, so this template requires efDataSize == 16 and desynchronises the extra-field chain on the 24- and 28-byte variants that real ZIP64 archives emit when the offset or disk number is also a sentinel. APPNOTE fixes both the order and the 8-byte width; a generator that must stay readable by this template should emit the two-field form and keep the header offset under 0xFFFFFFFF.

dependencies.description: EH_InfoZIPUnicodePath (0x7075) selects the Info-ZIP Unicode Path block, whose first byte is a version that is 1 in every implementation that exists.
dependencies.notes: Lines 239-244 read efVersion, efNameCRC32 and then efUnicodeName[efDataSize - 5]. Info-ZIP refuses a version it does not know and falls back to the plain frFileName, so pinning 1 keeps the UTF-8 name in use rather than silently discarded.

dependencies.description: Inside a 0x7075 block the Unicode name occupies exactly efDataSize - 5 bytes: the data size minus the 1-byte version and the 4-byte name CRC.
dependencies.notes: Line 243: 'char efUnicodeName[efDataSize - 5];' guarded by 'if(efDataSize > 0 )' at line 242, so efDataSize < 5 makes the template read a negative-length array; a generator must emit at least 5. EXTRAFIELD.efNameCRC32 must be the CRC-32 of the corresponding frFileName or deFileName bytes as emitted, which is the pairing Info-ZIP checks before trusting the UTF-8 name.

dependencies.description: EH_NTFS (0x000a) selects the NTFS block: a 4-byte reserved word followed by a chain of Tag/Size/data triples that must exactly fill efDataSize - 4 bytes.
dependencies.notes: Lines 245-261: 'int Reserved;', then 'local int len = efDataSize - 4;' and 'while (len > 0)' reading Tag and Size and decrementing len by Size + 4. The same while/len -= Size + 4 pattern as the outer extra-field chain, so an inner Size that overshoots desynchronises the rest of the header just as an outer efDataSize would.

dependencies.description: NTFS attribute tag 0x0001 is the file-times attribute and its data is exactly three 8-byte FILETIME values - last modification, last access, creation - instead of the generic byte blob.
dependencies.notes: Lines 252-257: 'if (Tag == 0x001) { FILETIME Mtime; FILETIME Atime; FILETIME Ctime; }' with the else arm at lines 258-259 reading 'byte Data[Size]'. So for tag 1 the enclosing EXTRAFIELD.Size must be 24 or the while(len > 0) loop at line 248 walks off the block.

dependencies.description: Any NTFS attribute tag other than 0x0001 carries Size bytes of opaque attribute data.
dependencies.notes: Lines 258-259: 'else byte Data[Size];'. Content is free - this is the Tier C side of the NTFS block - but the length is fixed by EXTRAFIELD.Size, which is Tier A because the loop counter depends on it.

dependencies.description: EH_StrongEncryption (0x0017) selects the strong-encryption header block: four 2-byte fields, then efDataSize - 8 bytes of certificate decryption data.
dependencies.notes: Lines 263-270 read Format, AlgID, Bitlen, Flags and then 'byte CertData[efDataSize - 8];' under 'if (efDataSize > 8)'. This is the extra-field copy of the in-record ZIPFILERECORD.StrongEncryptedHeader, and both are reachable, so the AlgID and Flags enumerations are recorded on both fields.

dependencies.description: EH_WzAES (0x9901) selects the WinZip AE block, whose data is always exactly 7 bytes: 2-byte version, 2-byte VendorID, 1-byte Strength, 2-byte real compression method.
dependencies.notes: Lines 271-276 read version, VendorID[2], Strength and deCompression with no length guard, so any other efDataSize desynchronises the extra-field chain at line 410 ('len -= frExtraField.efDataSize + 4;'). This block is mandatory whenever frCompression is 99: 99 is a marker, not a codec, and the real method is EXTRAFIELD.deCompression.

dependencies.description: Every other extra-field ID falls to the template's default arm and carries efDataSize bytes of opaque data.
dependencies.notes: Lines 277-280: 'default: if(efDataSize > 0 ) char efData[ efDataSize ];'. This covers the other 39 members of HEADERFLAG plus any unregistered ID, so the content is Tier C while the length stays Tier A through EXTRAFIELD.efDataSize. Note the five IDs listed are only the ones this template decodes - a real decoder knows several more (0x5455 extended timestamp, 0x7875 Info-ZIP UNIX new) and parses them, which is a divergence worth generating for.

dependencies.description: COMP_WzAES is not a codec: a 99 in the local header (or deCompression in the central directory) requires a WinZip AE extra field that names the method the payload is actually compressed with.
dependencies.notes: The .bt reads that method as EXTRAFIELD.deCompression at line 275 and branches on it nowhere else, so without the 0x9901 block the entry's real codec is undefined. WinZip AE also pairs version 2 (AE-2) with a zeroed frCrc/deCrc, which is recorded on those fields.

dependencies.description: COMP_STORED means the payload is the plaintext, so the compressed and uncompressed sizes must be identical and frCrc must be the CRC-32 of exactly those bytes.
dependencies.notes: The same equality applies to ZIPDIRENTRY.deCompressedSize / deUncompressedSize and to ZIPDATADESCR.ddCompressedSize / ddUncompressedSize when bit 3 of frFlags is set. Stored entries are the cheapest way to make a payload-dependent divergence reproducible, because the bytes on disk are the bytes the decoder reports.

dependencies.description: frFlags bit 11 (FLAG_UTF8Names, 0x0800) declares that frFileName, frExtraField's Unicode names and the comments are encoded in UTF-8.
dependencies.notes: With the bit clear the same bytes are CP437 and a decoder transcodes them; with it set a decoder passes them through and refuses or replaces invalid sequences. The .bt declares the field as char in both cases (line 404) and does not test the bit, so this is a spec-side rule that changes what the same bytes mean rather than what the template reads. Only the encoding is constrained - the characters themselves stay free.

dependencies.description: COMP_DEFLATE requires version needed to extract of at least 2.0.
dependencies.notes: APPNOTE 'Version Needed To Extract' table: 2.0 for deflate. The same rule applies to ZIPFILERECORD.frVersion. A lower value is not refused by any decoder - Info-ZIP warns and continues - which is why this stays Tier B and not Tier A.

dependencies.description: COMP_DEFLATE64 requires version needed to extract of at least 2.1.
dependencies.notes: APPNOTE table: 2.1 for Deflate64. Only Deflate64-capable decoders accept the method at all, so the version is the least of this entry's problems; it is still the rule a validator checks.

dependencies.description: COMP_BZip2 requires version needed to extract of at least 4.6.
dependencies.notes: APPNOTE table: 4.6 for BZIP2. Applies equally to ZIPFILERECORD.frVersion.

dependencies.description: COMP_LZMA (14) and COMP_PPMd (98) require version needed to extract of 6.3.
dependencies.notes: APPNOTE table: 6.3 for LZMA and for PPMd+. COMP_Jpeg (96) and COMP_WavPack (97) are WinZip additions with no version entry in the table, so no dependency is recorded for them; a generator emits 63 for those too and no decoder objects.

dependencies.description: COMP_WzAES requires version needed to extract of at least 5.1.
dependencies.notes: APPNOTE table: 5.1 for AES encryption, and the WinZip AE-1/AE-2 note specifies 51 for both AE versions, with EXTRAFIELD.version carrying 1 or 2 to distinguish them. Because 99 is a marker, the real codec in EXTRAFIELD.deCompression adds its own version requirement on top - a deflated AE entry still needs 51, and WinZip writes 51 rather than 20.

dependencies.description: DES (0x6601), original RC2 (0x6602), 3DES-168 (0x6603), 3DES-112 (0x6609) and RC4 (0x6801) strong encryption require version needed to extract of at least 5.0.
dependencies.notes: APPNOTE table lists 5.0 for DES, 3DES, original RC2 and RC4. The same requirement applies through EXTRAFIELD.AlgID when the strong-encryption header appears as extra field 0x0017 instead of inside the record.

dependencies.description: AES-128 (0x660E), AES-192 (0x660F), AES-256 (0x6610) and corrected RC2 (0x6702) require version needed to extract of at least 5.1.
dependencies.notes: APPNOTE table: 5.1 for AES and for corrected RC2, with 5.2 reserved for corrected RC2-64, which ALGFLAG does not give its own member - 0x6702 covers both and StrongEncryptedHeader.BitLen is what distinguishes the key size.

dependencies.description: Blowfish (0x6720) and Twofish (0x6721) strong encryption require version needed to extract of 6.3.
dependencies.notes: APPNOTE table: 6.3 for Blowfish and Twofish. AlgID_Unknown (0xFFFF) has no version entry, so no dependency is recorded for it.

dependencies.description: frFlags bit 5 marks the entry as compressed patched data, which requires version 2.7 and a Patch Descriptor extra field (0x000f).
dependencies.notes: APPNOTE: bit 5 set means the file is compressed patched data and requires PKZIP 2.70 or greater, with EH_PatchDescriptor (0x000f, line 161) carrying the patch metadata. Confidence is medium because the .bt names the bit FLAG_Reserved2 (line 118) and never tests it, so the template shows no trace of the rule - it is taken entirely from the specification. The bit is a legitimate generation target precisely because almost no decoder implements the patch-data set path.

dependencies.description: Any entry that uses ZIP64 format extensions - a ZIP64 extra field, or a 32-bit field carrying its sentinel - requires version needed to extract of at least 4.5.
dependencies.notes: APPNOTE table: 4.5 for ZIP64 format extensions. The same minimum applies to ZIPFILERECORD.frVersion, to ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64VersionToExtract and to deVersionMadeBy, whose upper byte additionally names the host system via VERECORD.HostOS.

dependencies.description: 0xFFFFFFFF in the central directory's uncompressed size is a sentinel, not a size: the entry must carry a ZIP64 extra field whose first 8 bytes are the true uncompressed size.
dependencies.notes: APPNOTE ZIP64 rule: the ZIP64 extra field holds only the values whose 32-bit counterparts are set to their maximum, in the fixed order uncompressed, compressed, relative header offset, disk start number. Lines 234 and 297 read efOriginalSize as the first uint64 in both EXTRAFIELD and EXTRA64FIELD. The same sentinel rule applies to ZIPFILERECORD.frUncompressedSize in the local header, which must also carry the ZIP64 field.

dependencies.description: 0xFFFFFFFF in the central directory's compressed size is a sentinel: the ZIP64 extra field must carry the true compressed size as its second 8-byte value.
dependencies.notes: Lines 235 and 298 read efCompressedSize as the second uint64. The template additionally uses this field as a skip distance in the top-level loop (lines 628-632: 'if (record.frExtraFieldLength > 0 && record.frExtraField.efHeaderID == EH_Zip64) FSkip(record.frExtraField.efCompressedSize);'), which is a template quirk - it treats the ZIP64 value as the payload length and skips it a second time, so a ZIP64 local header is mis-parsed by this .bt even when the file is correct. Recorded here because it is real evidence about how efCompressedSize is consumed.

then.section: EXTRAFIELD ZIP64 relative header offset (third 8-byte value)

dependencies.description: 0xFFFFFFFF in deHeaderOffset is a sentinel: the ZIP64 extra field must carry the true local-header offset as its third 8-byte value.
dependencies.notes: The template cannot show this rule: 'uint64 efHeaderOffset;' is commented out at lines 236 and 299, so a genuine ZIP64 archive whose offset is a sentinel is mis-parsed by this .bt (it reads only 16 of the 24 data bytes and then mis-counts the chain). Real decoders implement it, and the field is still recorded as Tier A on ZIPDIRENTRY.deHeaderOffset.

then.section: EXTRAFIELD ZIP64 disk start number (fourth 8-byte value)

dependencies.description: 0xFFFF in deDiskNumberStart is a sentinel: the ZIP64 extra field must carry the true disk number as its fourth 8-byte value.
dependencies.notes: 'uint efDiskNumberStart;' is commented out at lines 237 and 300, so like the header offset this rule is invisible to the template but binding on decoders. It only matters for genuinely split archives, which is why 0xFFFF here is a low-frequency but legal generation target.

dependencies.description: 0xFFFF in the end-of-central-directory entry count is the ZIP64 sentinel: a ZIP64 end record and its locator must precede this record, with ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64EntriesInDirectory carrying the true count.
dependencies.notes: APPNOTE ZIP64: the ZIP64 end of central directory record is required whenever any of the four 32-bit or 16-bit EOCD fields is set to its maximum, and the locator is what lets a decoder find it (it sits at a fixed 20 bytes before ZIPENDLOCATOR.elSignature). A sentinel with no ZIP64 tail is an immediate 'End-of-central-directory signature not found' or 'missing zip64 end record' from every decoder.

dependencies.description: 0xFFFF in the per-disk entry count is the ZIP64 sentinel; the true count lives in the ZIP64 end record.
dependencies.notes: For a single-volume archive elEntriesOnDisk equals elEntriesInDirectory, so both become 0xFFFF together and both ZIP64 counterparts must be present. The template's presence thresholds for those two fields differ (elr64DirectoryRecordSize > 12 for el64EntriesOnDisk and > 20 for el64EntriesInDirectory, lines 531-534), which only matters for a truncated ZIP64 end record.

dependencies.description: 0xFFFFFFFF in the central directory size is the ZIP64 sentinel; the true size lives in the ZIP64 end record.
dependencies.notes: The template reads el64DirectorySize only when elr64DirectoryRecordSize > 28 (line 535), and decoders read the true size from the ZIP64 record whenever the EOCD field is a sentinel; both must agree with the bytes actually emitted or the directory walk is truncated or overrun.

dependencies.description: 0xFFFFFFFF in the central directory offset is the ZIP64 sentinel; the true offset lives in the ZIP64 end record.
dependencies.notes: Template threshold: elr64DirectoryRecordSize > 36 (line 537). ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elDirectoryOffset must point at ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64Signature, and el64DirectoryOffset must point at the first ZIPDIRENTRY, so a generator writes three offsets that have to agree.

dependencies.description: The ZIP64 end of central directory locator exists only to point at the ZIP64 end of central directory record, so the record must be present and must end exactly where the locator's first byte begins.
dependencies.notes: The template's top-level loop accepts them in any order because it dispatches purely on the dword at the current offset (lines 649-658), so it cannot show the adjacency; APPNOTE fixes the layout as [ZIP64 end record][20-byte locator][EOCD]. dependencies.notes: Equivalently, a generator that decides to emit ZIP64 must emit both records, in this order, with the locator's elStartDiskNumber equal to ZIPENDLOCATOR.elStartDiskNumber and its elDirectoryOffset equal to the record's start offset.

dependencies.description: A ZIP64 end record larger than the fixed 44 bytes must carry the excess as extensible data sectors immediately after el64DirectoryOffset.

At exactly 44 the section is forbidden - emitting bytes there would be parsed as the next record's signature by the top-level loop. The commented-out EXTRA64FIELD chain at lines 542-547 shows the template's author intended to decode those sectors and did not.

dependencies.description: With HostOS 3 (OS_Unix) or 19 (OS_OSX), deExternalAttributes' high 16 bits are the POSIX file type and mode: kIFMT selects the type and the low 12 bits of that word are the permission bits.
dependencies.notes: The FILEATTRIBUTE members kIFMT / kIFDIR / kIFREG / kIFLNK ... kIXOTH at lines 332-356 are all shifted left by 16, so they only ever appear in the high word. Info-ZIP's mapattr() branches on the host OS before touching this field, which is why the same 32-bit value means two different things. The low byte still holds DOS attributes on most Unix writers, so both halves are commonly set at once.

dependencies.description: With HostOS 0 (OS_FAT), 6 (OS_HPFS), 11 (OS_NTFS) or 14 (OS_VFAT), deExternalAttributes' low byte is the DOS attribute set and the high word is ignored.
dependencies.notes: FA_READONLY through FA_VIRTUAL at lines 316-330 are the DOS bits; kIFMT and friends carry no meaning on this path. Info-ZIP mapattr() masks the high word away for these hosts, so a Unix mode written with HostOS 0 silently produces a file with no permission bits at all - a divergence worth generating deliberately.

dependencies.description: A nonzero name length requires exactly that many name bytes between the fixed header fields and the extra-field chain.

At zero the field is absent entirely, so no NUL terminator may be written - and conversely the name must not be NUL-terminated when the length is nonzero. ZIPDIRENTRY.deFileNameLength / deFileName (lines 499-500) work the same way, and the two names must match byte for byte for the same entry.

then.algorithm: sum of (efDataSize + 4) over every block equals frExtraFieldLength exactly

dependencies.description: A nonzero extra-field length requires a chain of header-ID/data-size/data blocks that exactly fills it.
