Because len is a signed int and the loop condition is len > 0, a block whose efDataSize + 4 overshoots the declared total drives len negative, ends the loop, and leaves the following bytes to be read as frData - the chain silently truncates instead of erroring. ZIPDIRENTRY.deExtraFieldLength uses the identical loop at lines 501-506.

dependencies.description: A nonzero comment length requires exactly that many comment bytes at the end of the central directory record.
dependencies.notes: Lines 507-508: 'if( deFileCommentLength > 0 ) uchar deFileComment[ deFileCommentLength ];'. It is the last variable part of the record, so a mismatch moves the start of the next ZIPDIRENTRY and every decoder then reports a bad signature. Content is Tier C; only the length is constrained.

dependencies.description: A zero archive comment length means the file ends with elCommentLength itself: no comment bytes and no trailing padding of any kind.
dependencies.notes: Lines 569-571 guard the comment with 'if( elCommentLength > 0 )'. Decoders additionally require (EOCD offset + 22 + elCommentLength) to equal the file size, so any byte after a zero-length comment makes the backward scan reject this record and search further back.

dependencies.description: A zero data length means the digital signature record is its 6-byte header alone, with no data bytes.
dependencies.notes: Lines 514-516: 'ushort dsDataLength; if( dsDataLength > 0 ) uchar dsData[ dsDataLength ];'. A record with dsDataLength 0 is legal and is the cheapest way to put the 0x05054b50 signature in the stream.

dependencies.description: With the data-descriptor bit set the local header's CRC and both sizes are written as zero, because they were not known when the header was emitted; the real values appear in the ZIPDATADESCR and in the central directory.
dependencies.notes: APPNOTE states the three fields are zeroed in the local header when bit 3 is set, and the .bt relies on it: line 462 tests 'frCompressedSize == 0 && (frFlags & FLAG_DescriptorUsedMask)' before scanning for the descriptor. A streaming entry that sets bit 3 but still writes real sizes is therefore mis-parsed by this template - it falls through all four frData branches and reads no payload at all - while most decoders tolerate it. That asymmetry is itself a good generation target.

dependencies.description: frFlags bit 13 (FLAG_CDEncrypted, 0x2000) declares that the central directory is encrypted and that selected local-header values are masked to hide their real contents.
dependencies.notes: Line 126 documents the bit; the template never tests it. APPNOTE says the masked fields hold values that must not be trusted, so on this path the local header ceases to be a cross-check against the central directory. Confidence is medium because no decoder in the reference set implements central-directory encryption, so the rule cannot be verified against behaviour.

dependencies.description: A strong-encryption header extra field implies frFlags bit 6; the block is the extra-field form of the same envelope the record carries inline.
dependencies.notes: APPNOTE: extra field 0x0017 is used with bit 6 of the general purpose bit flag. The template reads the extra-field copy unconditionally (line 263) and the in-record copy only when bits 0 and 6 are both set (line 415), so an extra-field 0x0017 with bit 6 clear parses but means nothing to a decoder.

dependencies.description: A WinZip AE extra field implies frCompression (and deCompression) of 99: the block is the marker's payload, and emitting it with any other method makes the entry's codec ambiguous.
dependencies.notes: The template's line 438 checks 'frExtraField.efHeaderID == EH_WzAES' inside the bit-0 + method-99 branch, so it only ever consults the block on that path. Decoders key off method 99 and then read the block; the reverse direction (block present, method not 99) is ignored by most and is a divergence to generate for.

dependencies.description: WinZip AE-2 sets both CRC fields to zero: integrity comes from the 10-byte HMAC-SHA1-80 authentication code instead of the CRC-32.
dependencies.notes: AE-1 (EXTRAFIELD.version 1) keeps the real CRC, AE-2 zeroes it; this is the one documented exception to frCrc and deCrc being the CRC-32 of the plaintext, and a generator that writes a real CRC into an AE-2 entry produces an archive WinZip itself flags as inconsistent while Info-ZIP ignores it.

then.pattern: the decompressed payload is apparently ASCII or text

dependencies.description: The low bit of the internal attributes declares that the entry apparently contains text rather than binary data.
dependencies.notes: APPNOTE: 'The lowest bit of this field indicates, if set, that the file is apparently an ASCII or text file. If not set, that the file apparently contains binary data.' Nothing in the template tests it (line 496 reads it and stops), and decoders use it only to decide whether to translate line endings, so the consequence is cosmetic rather than structural - hence Tier B on the field and a medium-confidence dependency. Setting it on a binary payload is a legal and cheap divergence.

dependencies.description: FA_DIRECTORY (0x00000010) marks the entry as a directory: conventionally its name ends with a slash, it has no payload, and its sizes and CRC are zero.
dependencies.notes: Info-ZIP and most other decoders decide 'is a directory' from the trailing slash in deFileName or from this bit, then skip extraction; a directory entry with a nonzero payload is still read, so the rule is a convention rather than a hard requirement, which keeps the fields themselves at their normal tiers. Version-needed 20 is the value writers pair with it (see VERECORD.Version value_names).

when.section: ZIPDATADESCR for an entry that also has a central directory record

then.required_value: equal to ZIPDIRENTRY.deCrc, deCompressedSize and deUncompressedSize for the same entry

dependencies.description: The data descriptor and the central directory must report the same three values for the entry they both describe.
dependencies.notes: The template stores them independently (lines 384-386 and 489-491) and never compares them, but Info-ZIP unzip does: a mismatch produces 'bad CRC' or a size warning and, for ddCompressedSize, a refusal to locate the following record. This is the streaming counterpart of the local-versus-central equality below.

then.required_value: byte-for-byte equal to the corresponding ZIPFILERECORD field of the same entry

dependencies.description: Every central directory record duplicates eight fields of its local header, and the duplicates must agree.
dependencies.notes: The duplication is the format's core redundancy: decoders read the central directory copy for listing and the local copy for extraction, then compare. deHeaderOffset is the link between them. Deliberate disagreement between the two copies is one of the highest-value ZIP mutations available, because each decoder picks a different side and reports a different file name, size or timestamp for the same entry.

then.required_value: the counts and byte ranges of the ZIPDIRENTRY series as actually emitted

dependencies.description: The four numbers in the end-of-central-directory record are derived from the archive itself: entries on this volume, entries in total, total directory bytes, and the offset of the first directory record.
dependencies.notes: These are the fields decoders use to find and bound their read of the directory, so a wrong elDirectoryOffset makes the whole archive unreadable even though every record in it is valid; a wrong elDirectorySize or count makes Info-ZIP stop early or read past the end into the ZIP64 tail. elEntriesOnDisk equals elEntriesInDirectory for a single-volume archive. All four must be computed after the directory is written, never guessed.

then.required_value: ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DiskNumber, the absolute offset of ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64Signature, and the total number of disks

dependencies.description: The ZIP64 locator exists solely to point at the ZIP64 end record: its offset is the real file position of that record's signature, its start disk is the disk the record lives on, and its third field is the total disk count (the .bt misnames it elEntriesInDirectory).
dependencies.notes: Decoders scan backwards from the EOCD for 0x07064b50, then seek to elDirectoryOffset; if that does not land on 0x06064b50 they abandon the ZIP64 path and fall back to the 32-bit values, silently truncating a large archive. The locator is 20 bytes and must sit immediately before the EOCD, so its own position is fixed once the entry and directory budgets are spent.

dependencies.description: The ZIP64 end record's size field counts the bytes that follow it, so the standard 56-byte record carries 44; only a record with extensible data sectors carries more.
dependencies.notes: The template's thresholds 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 20, 28, 36 and 44 (lines 523-539) are cumulative byte counts of the fixed part after the 12-byte signature-plus-size header, so 44 makes all eight fixed fields parse and no DataSect appear. Its el64EntriesOnDisk, el64EntriesInDirectory, el64DirectorySize and el64DirectoryOffset then hold the real 64-bit values that the EOCD sentinels stand in for.

when.section: the same EXTRAFIELD header ID present in both the local and the central copy of an entry

then.required_value: the block's payload must carry the same values in both copies; the two total lengths need not be equal

dependencies.description: Local and central extra-field chains describe the same entry, so a block that appears in both must say the same thing - but the two chains are separate byte ranges and may differ in length and membership.
dependencies.notes: frExtraFieldLength and deExtraFieldLength are independent fields read by independent loops (lines 406-411 and 501-506), and APPNOTE treats the central copy as the authoritative one for ZIP64 sentinels. Writers that put the ZIP64 block only in the central copy, or only in the local copy, are common and legal, which makes 'block present in one copy but not the other' a high-value divergence: decoders that read sizes from the local copy see 0xFFFFFFFF and report a corrupt entry, while decoders that read from the directory are fine.

then.note: has no comment field at all: comments exist only in the central directory

dependencies.description: Per-entry comments are a central-directory-only feature; the local header has frFileNameLength and frExtraFieldLength and no comment length, so deFileComment has no local counterpart to disagree with.
dependencies.notes: The asymmetry shows up in the structures themselves - ZIPFILERECORD ends after frData (line 470) while ZIPDIRENTRY carries deFileCommentLength and deFileComment (lines 507-508) - and it is why the archive-level comment lives in the EOCD while the entry-level one lives in the directory. A generator that tries to mirror a comment into the local header is inventing a field.

structure.subject: ZIPFILERECORD
structure.detail: The template's top-level loop starts at offset 0 (line 615 'while( !FEof() )' after 'LittleEndian();' at line 614), reads the first dword (line 618) and dispatches on it; the first record of a plain archive is a local file header matching S_ZIPFILERECORD at line 624. A dword that is none of the seven SignatureTYPE values hits the else at line 664 and aborts the whole parse with 'Unknown ZIP tag encountered. Template stopped.'
structure.description: A ZIP archive begins with a local file header whose signature is 0x04034b50.
structure.generation_note: emit ZIPFILERECORD as the first element, then the repeated entry array, then the directory, then the tail records.

structure.subject: self-extracting stub bytes before the first ZIPFILERECORD
structure.detail: Decoders locate the archive by scanning backwards from end-of-file for ZIPENDLOCATOR.elSignature and then compute (actual directory offset - elDirectoryOffset) as a stub delta, which they add to every deHeaderOffset; the template has no such compensation and dispatches on the dword at offset 0, so any prefix aborts it at line 666.
structure.description: Nothing may precede the first local file header for the template, while real decoders tolerate an arbitrary prefix.
structure.generation_note: emit no prefix in the default corpus; a deliberate stub is a separate, explicitly-flagged variant that only real decoders will accept.
structure.notes: This template-versus-decoder asymmetry is one of the few places where a legal file is unreadable by the .bt, so it belongs in the spec rather than being silently avoided.

structure.subject: ZIPENDLOCATOR (+ ZIPENDLOCATOR.elComment)
structure.detail: The end of central directory record is the last record: after it only elComment may follow, and only when elCommentLength > 0 (lines 569-571). The template's loop then sees FEof() and exits normally at line 615; any further bytes would be dispatched as another record and abort at line 666.
structure.description: The archive ends with the end-of-central-directory record and its optional comment, and with no trailing byte after that comment.
structure.generation_note: emit as a fixed tail: 22 bytes of EOCD fields, then elCommentLength comment bytes, then end of file.

structure.subject: ZIPENDLOCATOR
structure.detail: Every archive has exactly one end-of-central-directory record; it is the only record decoders require and the only one they can find without parsing the rest of the file. The template instantiates it in the S_ZIPENDLOCATOR branch at lines 659-663.
structure.description: The end-of-central-directory record is mandatory and appears exactly once.
structure.generation_note: always emit it, last, with counts and offsets derived from what was actually written.

structure.subject: ZIPFILERECORD + ZIPFILERECORD.frData + ZIPDATADESCR entry series
structure.detail: The number of entries is free, including zero: an empty archive is one ZIPENDLOCATOR with elEntriesOnDisk, elEntriesInDirectory, elDirectorySize and elDirectoryOffset all zero. The template's loop simply keeps dispatching until FEof() (line 615), so it imposes no count of its own.
structure.description: An archive contains zero or more entries, each a local header, its extra-field chain, its payload and an optional data descriptor.
structure.output_budget: Total file budget: 1 MiB (1048576 bytes) by default, held as a running total of bytes already written and charged against before each entry is emitted; stop adding entries when the next one would not fit. Fixed overhead always fits and is reserved first: 22 B EOCD, plus 64 B for the ZIP64 tail when it is used. The entry series gets the whole remainder - roughly 1 MiB minus the 64 KiB reserved for the central directory - because the payload is where the interesting bytes are. This is the only size control in the document: no field is capped to achieve it. If a derived payload would not fit in the remaining budget, redraw the plaintext and derive again rather than shrinking frUncompressedSize to a small fixed value.
structure.generation_note: emit a repeated array of entries bounded by output_budget, then the directory, then the tail.

structure.subject: ZIPFILERECORD series before ZIPDIRENTRY series
structure.detail: All local records and their payloads come first, then the central directory, then the ZIP64 tail, then the end-of-central-directory record. The template accepts any order because it dispatches on the dword at the current offset (lines 624-663), but ZIPDIRENTRY.deHeaderOffset is a backward pointer into the local series and ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDirectoryOffset points forward at the directory, so an interleaved layout cannot have both correct.
structure.description: The local record series precedes the central directory, which precedes the tail records.
structure.generation_note: emit local entries in order, recording each one's start offset, then emit the directory using those offsets, then the tail.

structure.subject: ZIPDIRENTRY series
structure.detail: The central directory is a dense run of ZIPDIRENTRY records with no padding, separators or alignment: elDirectoryOffset names its first byte, elDirectorySize its total, and elEntriesInDirectory its record count, so a gap breaks all three at once. The template walks it record by record in the S_ZIPDIRENTRY branch (lines 639-643).
structure.description: The central directory is a contiguous sequence of records spanning exactly elDirectorySize bytes.
structure.output_budget: Charged from the same 1 MiB running total: reserve 64 KiB for the directory before the entry series starts spending, because every entry owes one 46-byte record plus its name, extra fields and comment. A 64 KiB reserve fits roughly 700 minimal records or 100 typical ones, which is far more than the entry budget can produce, so the reserve is a floor that keeps the directory from ever being truncated. When it is exhausted, stop adding entries - never shorten a name or drop a deFileComment to make the directory fit.
structure.generation_note: emit the directory as a repeated array bounded by its output_budget, immediately after the last entry's payload or data descriptor.

structure.subject: ZIPDIRENTRY per ZIPFILERECORD
structure.detail: One central directory record per local record: elEntriesInDirectory counts the records and each record's deHeaderOffset points back at its ZIPFILERECORD.frSignature. APPNOTE requires a directory record for every entry in the archive; it does not require the two series to be in the same order, and duplicate names are legal.
structure.description: The directory has exactly one record per entry, and the counts in the end records must match it.
structure.generation_note: build the directory from the list of emitted local records, in any order, then write elEntriesInDirectory = list length and elDirectorySize = total bytes written.
structure.notes: Order mismatch between the two series is a legal and interesting variant: decoders that assume positional correspondence (some quick extractors and every naive fuzzer harness) read the wrong offsets, while Info-ZIP and libzip follow deHeaderOffset and stay correct.

structure.subject: ZIPDIRENTRY.deHeaderOffset → ZIPFILERECORD.frSignature
structure.detail: Each directory record must point at the first byte of the local header of the entry it describes. The template records both offsets independently (lines 402 and 498 store 'header offset' as a comment only, and deHeaderOffset is read as a plain integer) and never follows the pointer, but every decoder seeks to deHeaderOffset, checks that a local header signature is there, then reads frFileNameLength and frExtraFieldLength from that header to find where the payload starts.
structure.description: deHeaderOffset must land exactly on the corresponding ZIPFILERECORD.frSignature.
structure.generation_note: record the write position of each local header and reuse it verbatim as deHeaderOffset; do not derive it from the directory or from any size field.

structure.subject: ZIP64ENDRECORD + ZIP64ENDLOCATOR tail
structure.detail: The tail is required exactly when any of the 32-bit limits is hit - more than 65535 entries, a size or offset of 4 GiB or more, a comment longer than 65535 bytes - or whenever an 0x0001 extra field carries a ZIP64 sentinel. Its order is fixed: ZIP64ENDRECORD, then ZIP64ENDLOCATOR, then ZIPENDLOCATOR (template lines 650-658, and the elZ64ELOCOffset dependency). Without a sentinel nothing forces the tail to exist.
structure.description: The ZIP64 end record and its locator are required only when a ZIP64 sentinel appears, and they must appear immediately before the end-of-central-directory record, in that order.
structure.generation_note: decide once, up front, whether the archive will exceed any 32-bit limit or carry a sentinel; if not, omit both records entirely rather than writing zeroed placeholders.
structure.notes: Writing an all-zero ZIP64ENDRECORD when no sentinel is used is legal but adds 56 bytes of pure noise and, worse, teaches the reader that the tail is unconditional.

structure.subject: the four ZIPFILERECORD.frData branches
structure.detail: Exactly one of lines 415 (strong encryption), 435 (WinZip AES), 458 (frCompressedSize > 0) and 462 (data descriptor scan) can fire, because they are an if / else-if chain; if none matches, frData is absent and the entry has no payload at all.
structure.description: An entry's payload is read by exactly one of four mutually exclusive paths.
structure.generation_note: choose the payload shape from the entry's own frFlags, frCompression and frCompressedSize, then emit the bytes that path expects - one path per entry, never two.

structure.subject: bytes between ZIPFILERECORD.frData and ZIPDATADESCR when frFlags bit 3 is set
structure.detail: Nothing may separate the payload from its data descriptor, and the payload itself must not contain the dword 0x08074b50 unless ddCompressedSize is written to say where the descriptor really is. The template's recovery for this is a byte-at-a-time scan (lines 459-461, 'FindFirst( ddSignature )' after 'while( !FSeek( FTell() + 1 ) )'), which stops at the first occurrence anywhere in the file; a payload that happens to contain those four bytes is therefore truncated at that point and the remaining payload bytes are parsed as a new record.
structure.description: A data descriptor must follow its payload immediately, and the payload must not contain a false data-descriptor signature unless the compressed size names the real one.
structure.generation_note: when deriving a streaming entry, either keep the plaintext free of the 0x08074b50 pattern or write ddCompressedSize as the authoritative length; treat a payload that contains the pattern as a deliberate variant, not the default.
structure.notes: This is the single most fragile construct in the template - the scan is unbounded and silently consumes the rest of the archive - and the reason APPNOTE recommends always writing ddCompressedSize.

structure.subject: record signature outside the seven SignatureTYPE values
structure.detail: The dispatcher's else branch (lines 664-667) calls Printf and FSeek(0) / stops the template when the dword is not one of S_ZIPFILERECORD, S_ZIPDIGITALSIG, S_ZIPDATADESCR, S_ZIP64ENDRECORD, S_ZIP64ENDLOCATOR, S_ZIPDIRENTRY or S_ZIPENDLOCATOR. Every other dword, including the archive extra data record 0x08064b50 that APPNOTE permits, ends the parse.
structure.description: No dword at a record boundary may be anything other than one of the seven known signatures.
structure.generation_note: emit only known signatures at record boundaries; unknown-signal fuzzing is a mutation concern, not a generation one.
structure.notes: APPNOTE lists 0x08064b50 (archive extra data record, used to hold a PGP-style block before the first local header) as legal, and it is missing from SignatureTYPE at lines 69-82 - a real template gap worth recording so the divergence is intentional rather than accidental.

structure.subject: fields inside ZIPFILERECORD and ZIPDIRENTRY
structure.detail: Both records are a run of fixed-width fields followed by their variable parts in declaration order: ZIPFILERECORD is frSignature, frVersion, frFlags, frCompression, frFileTime, frFileDate, frCrc, frCompressedSize, frUncompressedSize, frFileNameLength, frExtraFieldLength, then frFileName, then the extra-field chain, then frData (lines 393-470); ZIPDIRENTRY is deSignature, deVersionMadeBy, deVersionNeeded, deFlags, deCompression, deFileTime, deFileDate, deCrc, deCompressedSize, deUncompressedSize, deFileNameLength, deExtraFieldLength, deFileCommentLength, deDiskNumberStart, deInternalAttributes, deExternalAttributes, deHeaderOffset, then deFileName, the extra-field chain and deFileComment (lines 476-508).
structure.description: Within a record the field order is fixed and the variable parts always come last, in name / extra / (comment /) data order.
structure.generation_note: emit the fixed fields first, then the variable parts in that order; never interleave them or move a length field after the bytes it counts.

structure.subject: frFileName, frExtraField chain, frData, deFileName, deExtraField chain, deFileComment, elComment, dsData
structure.detail: Every variable part is preceded by its own byte-count field, and the count covers that part only: frFileNameLength counts name bytes, frExtraFieldLength counts the whole chain including each block's 4-byte header, frCompressedSize counts payload bytes, deFileCommentLength counts comment bytes, elCommentLength counts the archive comment, dsDataLength counts signature data. There are no NUL terminators anywhere and no length-of-length fields.
structure.description: Each variable-length part is length-prefixed by a dedicated count field that appears earlier in the same record.
structure.generation_note: derive every payload first, then write its length into the prefix field and the bytes immediately after the fixed part; a length that counts the terminator, or omits a block header, is the most common way this format desynchronises.

structure.subject: EXTRAFIELD blocks inside one record's chain
structure.detail: Zero or more 4-byte-header blocks, read by 'while (len > 0)' (lines 406-411 locally, 501-506 centrally), each costing efDataSize + 4 bytes of the enclosing length field. Nothing requires any particular ID to appear, and unknown IDs are skipped as raw bytes by decoders and read as generic blocks by the template.
structure.description: An extra-field chain holds any number of blocks whose sizes sum exactly to the enclosing length field.
structure.output_budget: 4 KiB total across every extra-field chain, entry comment and archive comment in one file, charged to the same 1 MiB running total; that is roughly 80 maximum-size blocks or a few thousand small ones, well beyond what any single archive needs. When it is spent, stop adding blocks - never raise efDataSize to swallow the remaining bytes, and never pad a chain with a dummy block just to reach the declared length.
structure.generation_note: emit zero to a handful of blocks per record, drawn from the known ID set with unknown IDs mixed in, each with an efDataSize matching its own payload.

structure.subject: ZIPDIGITALSIG
structure.detail: Zero or more digital signature records, and they are not tied to the entry count: the template dispatches S_ZIPDIGITALSIG at any record boundary (lines 634-638) and reads dsDataLength bytes after the 6-byte header. APPNOTE describes the record as following the data it authenticates - after an entry's payload, or after the central directory - so its position is meaningful even though nothing enforces it.
structure.description: Digital signature records are optional, may appear at any record boundary the template can reach, and conventionally follow the data they sign.
structure.generation_note: emit at most a couple, either after an entry payload or after the directory, each with dsDataLength covering its own dsData; treat an unsigned archive as the default case.
structure.notes: A record placed after the central directory but before the ZIP64 tail is legal and is one of the few ways to put a known signature between the directory and the EOCD, which several decoders handle inconsistently.

structure.subject: ZIPFILERECORD.frData
structure.detail: The payload's byte count is set by the branch that reads it: 'uchar frData[ frCompressedSize ]' on the plain path (line 460), 'uchar frData[ frCompressedSize - 12 - lenSalt ]' on the WinZip AES path, which reserves 2 bytes for PassVerification and 10 for AuthenticationCode plus the salt (lines 453-456), and 'uchar frData[posNext - posCurrent]' on the descriptor path, which is whatever distance the scan found (line 471). The strong-encryption path at line 415 reads its own header, salt and payload instead.
structure.description: An entry's payload occupies exactly frCompressedSize bytes, less the AES envelope on the encrypted paths.
structure.generation_note: write frCompressedSize bytes of payload for a plain entry; for AES write salt + 2 + ciphertext + 10 and set frCompressedSize to that total.
structure.notes: Line 458's guard is '(frCompressedSize > 0) && (frCompressedSize < 0xFFFFFFFF)', so a local header carrying the ZIP64 sentinel 0xFFFFFFFF in frCompressedSize - perfectly legal when an 0x0001 block supplies the real size - falls through all four branches and the template reads no payload at all, then parses the entry's compressed bytes as records. Decoders substitute the ZIP64 value and extract normally. This is the sharpest template-versus-decoder divergence in the file and it is why the sentinel handling in dependencies is worth generating for rather than avoiding.

structure.subject: ZIPDATADESCR
structure.detail: Zero or one per entry, and only when frFlags bit 3 is set: the template instantiates it inside the descriptor branch at line 474, immediately after the scanned payload. With bit 3 clear there is no descriptor anywhere in the entry, and with bit 3 set but frCompressedSize nonzero the template never looks for one.
structure.description: A data descriptor is optional, appears at most once per entry, and appears only for streaming entries.
structure.generation_note: emit it directly after the payload of a streaming entry, as 12 or 16 bytes depending on whether ddSignature is present, and nowhere else.

structure.subject: padding, alignment or filler bytes between records
structure.detail: Every record is located either by sequential reading (the template's loop advances only by what each struct consumed) or by an offset field that counts real bytes from the start of the archive; there is no alignment requirement anywhere in the format and no field that expresses one.
structure.description: No byte may sit between two records that is not part of one of them.
structure.generation_note: emit records back to back; if extra space is wanted, put it in an extra-field block or a comment where a length field accounts for it.

structure.subject: any byte after ZIPENDLOCATOR.elComment
structure.detail: The archive ends with the comment. The template's loop condition '!FEof()' (line 615) means a further byte is dispatched as a record and aborts the parse at line 666; decoders compute the stub delta from (EOCD offset + 22 + elCommentLength) versus the file size, so trailing bytes either shift every offset in the archive or are silently ignored depending on the implementation.
structure.description: Nothing follows the end-of-central-directory comment.
structure.generation_note: make the EOCD comment the last thing written; if a trailing-garbage variant is wanted, generate it deliberately and expect decoders to disagree about every offset.

structure.subject: format-imposed count and offset limits
structure.detail: Without the ZIP64 extension the format caps: 65535 entries (elEntriesOnDisk / elEntriesInDirectory are ushort, lines 565-566), 65535 disks (elDiskNumber / elStartDiskNumber, lines 563-564, and deDiskNumberStart, line 503), 4 GiB - 1 for any size or offset (frCompressedSize, frUncompressedSize, deCompressedSize, deUncompressedSize, deHeaderOffset, elDirectorySize, elDirectoryOffset are uint), 65535 bytes for a file name, an extra-field chain, an entry comment or the archive comment (frFileNameLength, frExtraFieldLength, deFileCommentLength, elCommentLength are ushort), and 65535 bytes for one extra-field block's payload (efDataSize is ushort, line 246). Each cap is escaped by writing the sentinel 0xFFFF or 0xFFFFFFFF and supplying the real value in a ZIP64 extra field or the ZIP64 end record.
structure.description: Every count, size and offset field in ZIP is 16 or 32 bits wide, and the sentinel-plus-ZIP64 mechanism is the only way past those widths.
structure.generation_note: stay under the caps by default (the entry and directory output budgets keep the file far below them); use a sentinel only as a deliberate ZIP64 variant, always paired with the extra field or end record that carries the real value.
structure.notes: A sentinel written without its ZIP64 counterpart is the single most common corrupt-ZIP pattern in the wild, and decoders split on it: Info-ZIP reports 'zipfile is empty' or truncates the entry to 0 bytes, libzip reports an inconsistent archive, and Python zipfile happily seeks to offset 0xFFFFFFFF and raises OSError. Because the caps are wide, no field is narrowed to respect them.

diversity_axes.name: compression_method
diversity_axes.why: The single largest driver of decoder code in this format: it selects which decompressor is instantiated for the entry, and the choice cascades into frData's required structure, the minimum version, whether a data descriptor or an AES envelope is present, and which extra-field blocks mean anything.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Each method is a separate branch in every decoder: 0 copies bytes through, 8 calls inflate, 9 calls inflate with a 64 KiB window, 12 calls BZ2_bzDecompress, 14 parses the 9-byte ZIP LZMA header before calling the LZMA decoder, 98 initialises PPMd, 99 diverts to the WinZip AES path and reads the 0x9901 block first. Methods 1-7 and 18/19/96/97 take the 'unsupported compression method' error path, which is itself a distinct branch worth reaching. Python zipfile supports only 0 and 8 by default, so the same archive exercises different failure paths across decoders.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw from all 19 COMPTYPE members across the corpus, weighting 0 and 8 heavily because those are the two a generator can always emit correctly, and sprinkling 12, 14, 98, 99 and the unsupported values so every decoder branch is reached. Never fix it to 8 for the whole corpus.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: No separate budget: the method changes the payload's encoding, not its size ceiling. The entry series' share of the 1 MiB running total is what bounds the resulting bytes.
diversity_axes.notes: An unsupported method must still be paired with a legal frData byte count, because the decoder reads frCompressedSize to skip the entry even when it cannot decode it.

diversity_axes.name: central_compression_method
diversity_axes.why: The central copy of the method is what decoders read when listing, and it need not equal the local copy - that disagreement is a divergence in its own right, not an error to avoid by construction.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Info-ZIP uses deCompression for its listing and to choose the extractor before it reads the local header; libzip trusts the directory exclusively; Python zipfile reads the directory into ZipInfo and never re-checks the local method. A mismatch therefore changes which codec is invoked on the same bytes.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Equal to frCompression in the default corpus so the archive is coherent; drawn independently, from the same 19-member set, in a deliberate disagreement variant.
diversity_axes.notes: Listed separately from frCompression because the two fields are read by different decoder passes and the pairing is the interesting axis.

diversity_axes.name: general_purpose_bit_flags
diversity_axes.why: Sixteen independent bits, each of which enables or disables a subsystem: encryption, the streaming data descriptor, UTF-8 names, patch data, strong encryption, central-directory encryption, and the compression sub-options for deflate and implode. It is the second-largest path driver after the method.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Bit 0 sends the entry down the decryption path (and, with method 99, the AES path); bit 3 makes the decoder ignore the local CRC and sizes and look for a ZIPDATADESCR after the payload; bits 1-2 select deflate compression options and, for methods 6 and 10, the implode window size and tree count; bit 6 selects the strong-encryption header; bit 11 switches name decoding from CP437 to UTF-8; bit 13 declares the central directory encrypted; bits 14-15 mark patch data. Bit 5 says the entry is patched; bit 7 is reserved.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw combinations, not single bits: the default corpus covers {}, {3}, {11}, {3,11}, {0}, {0,6}; the wider corpus also reaches {13}, {5}, {14}, {15} and the deflate and implode sub-option bits. A corpus that only ever emits flags 0 exercises none of this.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: None needed: the flags are two bytes and cost nothing to vary.
diversity_axes.notes: Bits that change what other fields must contain (0, 3, 6, 11) have dependencies recorded; bits that are merely advisory (5, 13, 14, 15) are still emitted, because a decoder that honours them behaves differently.

diversity_axes.name: central_general_purpose_bit_flags
diversity_axes.why: The central copy of the flag word; decoders that only read the directory see this one and never the local copy, so bit 11 here decides whether a name is decoded as UTF-8 or CP437 during a plain listing.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Same bit meanings as frFlags, applied at listing time rather than extraction time; a bit-11 mismatch between the two copies is the classic mojibake divergence, and a bit-3 mismatch makes one decoder hunt for a data descriptor that the other ignores.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Equal to frFlags by default; drawn independently in the disagreement variant.
diversity_axes.notes: Kept as its own axis because the UTF-8 bit is read from here by every decoder that never opens the local header.

diversity_axes.name: entry_payload
diversity_axes.why: The format's only real payload and the reason ZIP has depth: its framing is pinned (frCompressedSize bytes, in the codec frCompression names) while its contents are entirely free, so a corpus can vary the plaintext and the encoding independently.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Method 0 hands the bytes straight to the caller; method 8 streams them through inflate, which validates block types, Huffman tables, length and distance pairs and the final-block flag; 12, 14 and 98 run their own decoders; 99 runs AES-CTR then HMAC verification. Malformed contents fail late and per entry, after the whole directory has been parsed.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw the plaintext freely - different lengths, shapes, entropies and byte alphabets per entry - then encode it with the selected method and measure. The plaintext, not the field, is the diversity source; a corpus whose payloads are all the same 16 bytes teaches a decoder nothing.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Charged to the entry series' share of the 1 MiB running total; the budget bounds how much payload there is, never what is inside it.
diversity_axes.notes: content_is_free is true on the constraint entry: pin the envelope, free the contents.

diversity_axes.name: uncompressed_size
diversity_axes.why: Derived, never chosen: it is the byte length of the plaintext the payload decodes to. It is listed here because it is exactly the field a size-conscious author would be tempted to pin to something small, which is the GIF mistake - pinning it would collapse the payload axis and with it the whole point of the entry.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: inflate output-length checks, the preallocation size in every decoder, the 'incorrect length of compressed data' comparison, and the ZIP64 sentinel test that diverts to the 0x0001 extra field.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Follows the free plaintext: compute it as len(plaintext) after drawing the plaintext, and let the output budget be the only thing that bounds it. Values span the whole uint32 range in principle, plus the 0xFFFFFFFF sentinel on the ZIP64 path.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: No separate budget; it is a measurement of bytes the entry series' 1 MiB share already paid for.
diversity_axes.notes: Never invent a size and then emit that many bytes of something else: build the payload, then measure it.

diversity_axes.name: compressed_size
diversity_axes.why: Also derived - it is the length of the encoded payload, and on the encrypted paths the length of the whole envelope. It doubles as the field that decides which of the template's four frData branches fires, so varying it varies the parse path, not just the byte count.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The number of bytes read or skipped per entry; the boundary that separates one entry's payload from the next record; the streaming test (zero plus frFlags bit 3) that makes a decoder look for a data descriptor; and the ZIP64 sentinel test.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Measure the encoded payload and write that number; zero only on the streaming path, 0xFFFFFFFF only on the deliberate ZIP64 path. It varies because the plaintext and the codec vary.
diversity_axes.notes: The template's line-458 guard '(frCompressedSize > 0) && (frCompressedSize < 0xFFFFFFFF)' means the sentinel value takes the no-payload path there while decoders substitute the ZIP64 value - recorded in structure[].requires for frData.

diversity_axes.name: crc32
diversity_axes.why: A checksum over the plaintext, so it is computed rather than drawn; it is listed as an axis only to say explicitly that it must not be pinned to a constant, because a constant CRC forces a constant plaintext and quietly kills the payload axis.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Compared against the CRC of the decompressed bytes at the end of extraction in every decoder; the WinZip AE-2 exception zeroes it and moves integrity checking to the 10-byte AuthenticationCode.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Compute CRC-32/ISO-HDLC over the plaintext (Python zlib.crc32) and write it; zero on the streaming path and on AE-2. It varies with the payload.
diversity_axes.notes: A wrong-but-legal CRC is a mutation target, not a generation target: generated files carry the correct CRC so decoders get all the way to the end of extraction.

diversity_axes.name: file_name_length
diversity_axes.why: Derived from the name it prefixes, but it is the axis that decides how much of the name space the corpus covers: a fixed short name for every entry hides every path-length, traversal and encoding branch a decoder has.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Buffer sizing and the path-sanitisation pass in every decoder (leading and embedded slashes, '..' components, backslashes, drive letters, control bytes, over-long names, names at the 65535-byte cap), plus the UTF-8 versus CP437 decode selected by frFlags bit 11, and the directory-entry test (trailing slash).
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw the name freely - empty, one byte, deep directory trees, names with spaces, dots, non-ASCII UTF-8, CP437 bytes with bit 11 clear, names ending in a slash for directory entries, names at the length cap - then write its byte length. Vary names across entries within one file as well as across files.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Names and comments share the 4 KiB extra-field/comment budget in structure[].cardinality, charged to the same 1 MiB running total; when it is spent, stop adding entries rather than shortening a name.
diversity_axes.notes: The two copies of a name (local and central) must be byte-identical by default; making them differ is a deliberate divergence variant, not the default.

diversity_axes.name: central_file_name_length
diversity_axes.why: The copy decoders actually show to the user, and the one libzip and Python zipfile trust without reading the local header at all; varying it independently of frFileNameLength is what exposes the trust difference.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Listing output, the extraction target path, the duplicate-name and case-collision handling, and the directory-versus-file decision (trailing slash or deExternalAttributes FA_DIRECTORY).
diversity_axes.how_varied: Equal to frFileNameLength with the same bytes by default; independently drawn in the disagreement variant so one decoder extracts under one name and another under a different one.
diversity_axes.notes: deFileCommentLength and deFileComment are separate axes below; the name is the one every decoder touches.

diversity_axes.name: extra_field_length
diversity_axes.why: It bounds a whole repeating sub-structure, so it is the axis that decides how many extra-field blocks the corpus exercises; pinning it to zero would delete the ZIP64, Unicode-path, NTFS-timestamp and AES subsystems from every generated file.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The chain walk itself, then a per-ID dispatch in every decoder: 0x0001 supplies ZIP64 sizes and offsets, 0x7075 overrides the name with a UTF-8 copy plus a CRC of the original, 0x000a carries NTFS timestamps, 0x0017 carries the strong-encryption header, 0x9901 carries the WinZip AE version and strength; unknown IDs take the skip-and-ignore path.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Zero for plain entries; otherwise the exact sum of (efDataSize + 4) over the blocks drawn, which is what makes the count vary from 4 bytes to the 65535-byte cap. Vary block count, block order, and whether a block appears at all.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: The 4 KiB extras-and-comments share recorded in structure[].cardinality for EXTRAFIELD blocks.
diversity_axes.notes: The template's signed-int loop ('while (len > 0)', lines 406-411) silently truncates a chain whose last block overshoots the declared total - a divergence to generate for deliberately.

diversity_axes.name: central_extra_field_length
diversity_axes.why: The central chain is where ZIP64 values are authoritative for most decoders, so a corpus that only puts blocks in the local chain tests a different set of paths than one that puts them in both, or only in the central one.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Same per-ID dispatch, applied at listing time; libzip and Python zipfile read ZIP64 sizes and deHeaderOffset replacements from here exclusively.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Independent of the local chain: same blocks, a subset, a superset, or completely different membership. The sum rule is identical.
diversity_axes.notes: Recorded separately because the two chains are separate byte ranges with separate length fields and separate decoder passes.

diversity_axes.name: extra_field_id
diversity_axes.why: The extra-field vocabulary: which ID a block carries decides which optional subsystem the entry has, and 44 IDs are named in the template's HEADERFLAG enum plus an open-ended space of unregistered ones.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A per-ID switch in every decoder (0x0001 ZIP64, 0x0007, 0x0008, 0x000a NTFS times, 0x5455 extended times, 0x7075 Unicode path, 0x7855 Unix UID/GID, 0x0017 strong encryption, 0x9901 WinZip AE, 0x4690 POSZIP, and so on), plus the default 'unknown ID, skip efDataSize bytes' path that every conforming decoder must take.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw from the 44 named IDs plus invented unregistered ones (both the 0x0000-0x7fff 'public' space and the 0x8000-0xffff private space), several blocks per entry, in varying order, with duplicates and with a block whose efDataSize disagrees with what its ID normally carries.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Charged to the 4 KiB extras-and-comments share.
diversity_axes.notes: Unknown IDs are not an error case: skipping them correctly is a decoder behaviour worth covering on every file.

diversity_axes.name: extra_block_size
diversity_axes.why: The stride of the chain walk: every block's size decides where the next block starts, so varying it varies the chain shape and, when it disagrees with the ID's usual layout, exposes the decoders that trust the ID over the size.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The 'skip this many bytes' arithmetic in the unknown-ID path, and the length validation in the known-ID paths (0x0001 requires a multiple of 8 and at least the fields whose sentinels are set; 0x7075 requires at least 5; 0x9901 requires exactly 7).
diversity_axes.how_varied: Measure the block's payload and write that number, including the deliberately odd cases: zero-length blocks, blocks whose payload is shorter or longer than the ID's documented layout, and blocks padded so the chain total still matches the enclosing length.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Shares the 4 KiB extras-and-comments budget; a maximum-size block is 65535 bytes, so the budget, not the field, is what limits the corpus.
diversity_axes.notes: The block contents (efData and the typed sub-fields) are Tier C and free; only this stride is pinned.

diversity_axes.name: version_needed_and_version_made_by
diversity_axes.why: Both version fields declare which feature set the entry uses, and decoders compare them against the features they actually find; the low byte is the APPNOTE version number and the high byte is the host system.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 'Zip data descriptor not supported' / 'unsupported compression method' style refusals when the declared version exceeds what the decoder implements, the ZIP64 gate at 45, the deflate64 gate at 21, the directory-entry convention at 20, the Unicode-path and AE gates at 50-63, and the host byte that selects DOS versus Unix interpretation of deExternalAttributes.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Cover the full documented set {10, 11, 20, 21, 25, 27, 45, 46, 50, 51, 52, 61, 62, 63} across the corpus, paired with the host byte, and honour the per-method minimums recorded in dependencies; also emit versions below the minimum for a method as a deliberate divergence.
diversity_axes.notes: Version 10 on a deflated entry is the most common real-world lie in ZIP files, and decoders split on whether to honour it.

diversity_axes.name: host_system
diversity_axes.why: It reinterprets a neighbouring field: the same 32 bits of deExternalAttributes mean DOS attribute bits on hosts 0, 6, 11 and 14 and a Unix mode_t on hosts 3 and 19, so this byte changes what the decoder does with bytes it has already read.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Info-ZIP switches its whole attribute-translation table on the host byte (permission bits, file type, FAT attributes, NTFS/OS2 special cases); libzip uses it to decide whether to apply a umask; Python zipfile exposes it raw and lets the caller interpret.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw from all 20 documented host values (0-19) across the corpus, not just 3 (Unix) and 0 (MS-DOS), and pair each with deExternalAttributes bytes that mean something on that host.
diversity_axes.notes: Values above 19 are undefined by the APPNOTE; emitting them is a legal-but-uninterpreted divergence rather than an error.

diversity_axes.name: external_file_attributes
diversity_axes.why: A 32-bit field whose meaning is entirely a function of VERECORD.HostOS, with 44 named bits in the template's FILEATTRIBUTE enum: nine DOS attribute bits, the Unix file-type bits in the high word, nine permission bits, and the reserved aliases.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The chmod applied on extraction, the directory test (FA_DIRECTORY 0x10 or S_IFDIR 0x40000000), the read-only and hidden tests that change whether a file can be overwritten, symlink and device-file creation on Unix hosts, and the 'is this a volume label or a subdirectory' branches on DOS hosts.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw combinations per host: Unix mode words covering regular files with several permission sets, directories, symlinks and setuid bits; DOS words covering read-only, hidden, system, directory, archive and volume-label bits; and words that mix the two conventions.
diversity_axes.notes: A symlink mode with a nonzero payload, or FA_DIRECTORY with a trailing-slash-less name, are both legal and both divergent - decoders disagree about which signal wins.

diversity_axes.name: internal_file_attributes
diversity_axes.why: Two documented bits - the low one says the entry is apparently text, the high one says the file was created with an application that left the high bit of a byte set - and everything else reserved; small, cheap to vary, and honoured differently by every decoder.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The EBCDIC/text-translation decision in Info-ZIP (which can rewrite line endings on extraction), the 'is binary' heuristic in tools that decide whether to display a file, and the reserved bits that most decoders ignore entirely.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit 0, 1, 2, 3 and reserved-bit combinations across the corpus, deliberately including bit 0 set on binary payloads and clear on text payloads.
diversity_axes.notes: Medium-confidence dependency recorded in dependencies[]; the consequence is cosmetic, which is why the field is Tier B rather than A.

diversity_axes.name: local_header_offset
diversity_axes.why: The link between the two halves of the format: every decoder that extracts (rather than merely lists) seeks to this offset. It is derived from where the local header was actually written, and pinning it to a constant would make multi-entry archives unreadable rather than diverse.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The seek that precedes every local-header read, the stub-delta computation (real directory offset minus elDirectoryOffset) that self-extracting archives depend on, the ZIP64 replacement path when the value is the 0xFFFFFFFF sentinel, and the 'expected local header signature, found something else' check.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Record the write position of each local header and reuse it; it varies naturally with entry count, name lengths, extra fields and payload sizes. The sentinel 0xFFFFFFFF appears only on the ZIP64 variant.
diversity_axes.notes: Offsets that are correct-but-shifted by a constant (the stub case) are a separate deliberate variant, since decoders differ on whether they compensate.

diversity_axes.name: entry_count_and_directory_extents
diversity_axes.why: The four EOCD numbers are the decoder's map of the archive; they are derived from what was written, and they must vary with the entry count rather than being fixed at 1, because a corpus of single-entry archives never reaches the multi-record directory code.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The loop bound over the directory, the byte budget that stops a decoder reading past the directory into the ZIP64 tail, the seek to the first record, and the sentinel tests that divert each of them to its ZIP64 counterpart.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Count and measure after writing: zero entries for the empty-archive case, one, a handful, and as many as the 64 KiB directory reserve allows. Sentinels (0xFFFF / 0xFFFFFFFF) appear only on the ZIP64 variant, always with their 64-bit counterparts filled in.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: The 64 KiB directory reserve in structure[].contiguous is what bounds the count, charged to the same 1 MiB running total; it is never bounded by capping this field.
diversity_axes.notes: An entry count that disagrees with the number of records actually present is the highest-value ZIP divergence available and belongs in the mutation set, not the generation set.

diversity_axes.name: data_descriptor
diversity_axes.why: Whether an entry has a trailing descriptor at all, whether it carries the optional 4-byte signature, and whether its three numbers are 32- or 64-bit: this is the streaming-write path and the reason a decoder can be forced to scan rather than trust the local header.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: frFlags bit 3 makes the decoder skip the local CRC and sizes; it then either reads the descriptor at the offset the central size implies or scans forward for 0x08074b50; the presence or absence of the signature decides which of the two layouts is parsed, and the 64-bit layout is selected by the same sentinel test as everywhere else. Info-ZIP, libzip and Python zipfile disagree about whether the signature is required.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Four variants across the corpus: no descriptor (bit 3 clear), descriptor with signature, descriptor without signature, and the 64-bit form. When a descriptor is present the local CRC and both sizes are zeroed and the true values live in the descriptor and in the central record, which must agree.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: 12 or 24 bytes per entry; free within the budget.
diversity_axes.notes: A payload whose first four bytes are 0x08074b50 makes signature-scanning decoders stop early - a legal, cheap, high-value divergence. The template declares only the 32-bit ddCRC, ddCompressedSize and ddUncompressedSize; the ZIP64 descriptor is those same three members widened to 8 bytes under the sentinel test, so it needs no separate keys.

diversity_axes.name: modification_timestamp
diversity_axes.why: A DOS date/time pair duplicated into the central record, with optional sub-second and Unix/NTFS precision carried in extra fields; every decoder reads it, several convert it, and none of them validate it the same way.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The MS-DOS-to-unix conversion (16-bit fields, month 1-12, day 1-31, two-second resolution), the out-of-range month/day handling, the pre-1980 clamp, the 1980-versus-2107 saturation, the 0x000a NTFS 100-nanosecond FILETIME path, the 0x5455 extended-time path, and the 'restore mtime on extraction' code that can fail or silently skip.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw dates spanning 1980 to the present plus deliberate edge cases (all-zero, month 0, month 13, day 32, hour 24, year 127, the 2107 saturation), and vary whether the local and central copies agree and whether a sub-second extra field contradicts them.
diversity_axes.notes: Purely cosmetic for the payload, but it is one of the few places where decoders disagree loudly while both remaining 'correct'.

diversity_axes.name: archive_comment_and_entry_comment_lengths
diversity_axes.why: The archive comment length is what makes the EOCD findable: decoders scan backwards from the end of the file for 0x06054b50 and use this field to confirm they have the last one, so its value changes where the archive is considered to end.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The backwards scan window (65535 + 22 bytes), the self-extracting-stub tolerance, the 'comment claims more bytes than remain' rejection, and the entry-comment read path that only fires when deFileCommentLength is nonzero.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Empty by default; then a few bytes, a sentence, and a maximum-size 65535-byte comment. Entry comments only exist in the central record and are drawn independently, including a nonzero length with an empty string and vice versa.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Charged to the 4 KiB extras-and-comments share; a maximum-size comment consumes it entirely, so at most one such file per corpus.
diversity_axes.notes: Comment bytes are free content (Tier C); only the length prefix is derived.

diversity_axes.name: encryption_and_aes_envelope
diversity_axes.why: Encryption is a cross-cutting variant rather than a single field: it changes the meaning of frData, forces frFlags bit 0, changes frCrc handling, and on method 99 adds a 0x9901 block plus a salt and an HMAC around the payload. The AES strength byte is the anchor because it is the one value that selects the envelope's size.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Traditional PKWARE decryption (12-byte header, three 32-bit keys seeded from CRC and time, check-byte verification), the AES path (salt length 8/12/16 by strength, 2-byte password verifier, AES-CTR payload, 10-byte HMAC-SHA1-80 trailer, AE-1 keeps the CRC while AE-2 zeroes it), the strong-encryption header path at frFlags bit 6, and the certificate-list path for central-directory encryption at bit 13.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Unencrypted by default; then each of the three AES strengths (1, 2, 3) with AE-1 and AE-2; then traditional PKWARE encryption on a non-99 method; then the strong-encryption header variant; then central-directory encryption with a certificate list. Vary the password (short, long, empty, non-ASCII) since the salt and verifier depend on it.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Envelope overhead is 12 bytes (PKWARE) or salt+2+10 bytes (AES), plus the 0x9901 block's 11 bytes, charged to the entry's payload share.
diversity_axes.notes: frCompressedSize must count the whole envelope - salt, verifier, ciphertext and HMAC - because that is what sits between the local header and the next record.

diversity_axes.name: zip64_tail_presence
diversity_axes.why: Whether the ZIP64 end-of-central-directory record and its locator exist at all is a file-level axis: their presence moves the EOCD away from the end of the file, and every 64-bit value in the format is only reachable through them.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The backwards scan that must look 20 + 56 bytes further when the tail is present, the sentinel tests on five fields that divert to the tail, the 'ZIP64 record present but no sentinels set' tolerance, and the version-45 gate that some decoders enforce only when the tail exists.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Absent by default for small archives; present with sentinels in exactly the fields whose 64-bit values are needed; present with sentinels in every field; present but with no sentinels anywhere (the tolerance case); present with a nonzero DataSect (the extensible-data-sector case).
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: 76 bytes fixed (56 + 20) plus the 4-byte header when present; negligible.
diversity_axes.notes: The tail must sit immediately before the ZIP64 locator, which must sit immediately before the EOCD, with the locator's offset pointing at the tail - three orderings the template only checks pairwise.

diversity_axes.name: entry_count_and_file_layout
diversity_axes.why: The file-level layout axis: how many entries, in what order, with what interleaving of local records, descriptors, payloads, digital signatures, directory records and the tail. It is anchored to the local-header signature because that signature marks the start of each entry and is what every scanning decoder searches for.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The forward sequential scan some tools do (following local signatures), the directory-driven random-access path others do (following deHeaderOffset), the recovery path that falls back to scanning when the directory is unusable, the digital-signature skip, and the stub / archive-comment tolerance at both ends of the file.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Vary the entry count from 0 to as many as the budget allows; vary ordering (sorted names, random names, directory entries before their children, directory entries after, duplicate names); vary the multi-disk fields; and include one file with a digital signature record and one with a self-extracting stub before the first local header.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: This axis spends the 1 MiB total: 64 KiB reserved for the directory, 4 KiB for extras and comments, the remainder for entry series and payloads. When the budget is exhausted, stop adding entries; never shrink a name, extra field or payload to fit one more.
diversity_axes.notes: Entry count is the single highest-leverage axis in the format: a corpus of only single-entry archives leaves the directory walk, the offset arithmetic and the count validation entirely untested.
